Satisfactory healing is noted following repair of the quadriceps tendon.

Osteochondral loose body in the medial parapatellar recess of the joint, detached from the patella.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Patient reports history of chondroblastoma to the right knee diagnosed in <[YEAR]> but not fully worked up. X-ray in <[Month]> <[YEAR]> confirms nonspecific lytic lesion right patella. Please assess.

PRIOR IMAGING: Plain film radiographs from [Date]
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

In the superolateral aspect of the patella there is a T2 bright focus with irregular sclerotic margination seen on the plain film characterized by low signal margination on MRI. This focal lesion has central T2 bright signal similar in signal to articular cartilage and has a linear cartilaginous signal extending posteriorly to the articular surface of patella. The articular cartilage of patella directly posterior to this focus is intact but does demonstrate slight contour irregularity and signal change which may represent mild chondrosis. The finding measures about 1 cm in maximum diameter. The appearance is typical in location and MRI features of a dorsal defect of the patella. This represents a normal anatomic variant.

Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable. The TT-TG distance measures about 1.5 cm, at the upper limits of normal, consistent with an element of mild lateralization of the tibial tubercle

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

Within the lateral femoral condyle there is a serpiginously marginated lesion measuring 2.1 AP, 1.4 cm with an 0.9 cm in depth situated 2 to 3 mm deep to the cortex of the lateral femoral condyle. The rim of this lesion is T2 bright and T1 dark with central fat. MR features are typical of a bone infarct. No evidence of cortical collapse.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a trace Baker's cyst demonstrated. No significant knee effusion is demonstrated.

A few small subcentimeter popliteal lymph nodes are incidentally noted.

Marrow signal is otherwise normal. No other bone infarcts are seen within field-of-view.

INTERPRETATION: 
Subcortical chondroid focus in the superolateral aspect of patella has MR features typical of a dorsal defect of the patella. The finding is not typical of a chondroblastoma. Mild overlying chondromalacia patella.

Mild lateralization of tibial tubercle.

Trace Baker's cyst.

There is a bone infarct seen in the lateral femoral condyle. No evidence of articular collapse.
Clinical correlation as to the possible cause of a bone infarct in this patient is recommended.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
Degeneration is observed in the medial meniscus with a degree of subluxation.
The lateral meniscus, cruciate and collateral ligaments, as well as the articular cartilage of the medial and lateral compartments do not show pathological findings.
On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, fraying as well as thinning ICRS grade II are observed in the articular cartilage of the medial facet of the patella.
A significant joint effusion is observed intra-articularly with extension into the suprapatellar recess.

There is a small Baker's cyst. There is edema and fluid seen around the pes anserine tendons consistent with pes anserine bursitis.

There is a small knee effusion. Mild reactive synovitis is noted.

Marrow signal is within normal limits.

Mild tricompartmental chondrosis with early degenerative spurring to the lateral joint margin.

Small Baker's cyst.

Pes anserine bursitis.

The patella is laterally subluxed and there is diffuse edema seen along the course of the medial patellofemoral ligament consistent with a high-grade injury. This extends to the femoral attachment and also involves the attachment at the patella. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact and appears unremarkable.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment appears to be well maintained.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is mild intrinsic signal within the posterior cruciate ligament but intact fibers are present and the signal changes may in part be artifactual.

There is edema around the proximal and mid fibers of the medial collateral ligament consistent with low-grade medial collateral ligament sprain.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon, popliteus tendon and IT band all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small to moderate knee effusion. There is no Baker's cyst demonstrated.

Torn medial patellofemoral ligament associated with bone contusions an osteochondral fracturing of the medial surface of patella and lateral femoral condyle associated with transient dislocation of the patellofemoral joint.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Background changes of lateralization of the tibial tubercle and shallowness of the trochlear groove predisposing to patellar dislocation.

Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
Grade III degeneration and a horizontal tear in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus were observed. Volume loss is noted in the medial meniscus, which appears mildly extruded. Maceration is present in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, with significantly decreased anterior horn volume and a complex tear. The signal of the anterior cruciate ligament is mildly diffusely increased (myxoid degeneration). The posterior cruciate ligament is normal. The area surrounding the lateral collateral ligament appears markedly edematous with focal irregularities in places (grade II sprain). Edematous appearance was observed around the medial collateral ligament (grade I sprain). Widespread fluid increases were observed in the suprapatellar bursa and within the knee joint. Osteophytic spurs were observed in the bony structures forming the knee joint. Bone marrow edema and subchondral sclerosis findings were observed at the level of the lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau. Loss of cartilage integrity and joint space narrowing were observed (degenerative arthritis). A lobulated-contoured Baker's cyst measuring 80x25 mm was observed in the popliteal fossa. The subcutaneous fatty tissue at the prepatellar level of the knee joint appears edematous. Several ganglion cysts, the largest measuring 20x8 mm, were observed adjacent to the tendon insertion at the level of the medial crus of the gastrocnemius.

ACL.evidence: No mention of the ACL anywhere in the report; the study focuses on patellar tracking, synovitis, and effusion. Absence of any ACL comment in a knee with massive effusion and possible post-traumatic aetiology leaves a small residual chance, but nothing supports a tear.

MCL.evidence: The report describes 'Laxity of medial patellar retinaculum with mild increased signal intensity, R/O grade 2 injury,' which is the medial PATELLAR retinaculum (extensor mechanism), not the medial collateral ligament. The MCL itself is never mentioned.

Medial Meniscus.evidence: No meniscal pathology is described anywhere in the report. The study is dominated by effusion, synovitis, and patellar findings. Silent on the medial meniscus; base-rate probability applies.

Lateral Meniscus.evidence: No mention of the lateral meniscus. The report does not describe any meniscal tear or degenerative signal. Base-rate probability.

Medial OA.evidence: Only 'Tiny subchondral cysts in tibial eminence' are noted; no medial compartment cartilage loss, full-thickness defect, or bone-on-bone change is described. Tiny subchondral cysts at the eminence do not constitute medial compartment OA.

Lateral OA.evidence: The 'Increased signal intensity of articular cartilage at lateral facet' refers to the lateral patellar facet (patellofemoral joint), not the lateral tibiofemoral compartment. No lateral compartment cartilage loss is described.

PF OA.evidence: 'Increased signal intensity of articular cartilage at lateral facet, R/O grade 1 chondromalacia.' Grade 1 chondromalacia represents mild signal change/softening without substantial cartilage loss; per scoring rules this is well below grade 3-4 chondropathy, warranting a low-moderate probability (~0.3).

Effusion.evidence: 'Massively increased joint effusion and extending to proximal tibiofibular joint' and impression: 'Synovitis of knee joint with massive joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis.' The word 'massive' places this firmly in the large/massive category (≥0.92).

Synovitis.evidence: 'hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis; Prominent suprapatellar bursitis' and impression: 'Synovitis of knee joint with massive joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis.' Synovial hypertrophy with bursitis is explicitly diagnosed.

Baker's.evidence: No popliteal or Baker's cyst is mentioned. The effusion extends to the proximal tibiofibular joint, but a discrete popliteal cyst is not described. Not explicitly excluded; mild upward adjustment from base rate given the massive effusion.

Contusion.evidence: 'Increased infiltration in the muscle of popliteus muscle and intermuscular infiltration, R/O mild myositis' and 'Mild fat stranding along proximal portion of patellar tendon and infrapatellar fat plane, maybe due to inflammation or post arthrocentesis change.' These are described as inflammatory/myositis or post-procedural rather than traumatic bone bruise; no classic traumatic marrow oedema pattern is reported.

Fracture.evidence: No fracture is described. 'Tiny subchondral cysts in tibial eminence' are degenerative cystic changes, not fractures. No cortical disruption, avulsion, or insufficiency fracture is mentioned.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
No pathological findings are observed on evaluation of the medial and lateral compartments, including the menisci.
In the region of the tibial epiphysis, particularly lateral to the midline, there are confluent small cystic lesions with a total transverse diameter of 2.5 cm with surrounding edema.
The cruciate and collateral ligaments have normal morphology.
On evaluation of the anterior compartment and the extensor mechanism, there is degeneration of the articular cartilage (ICRS grade 4) at the inferior lateral aspect of the patella with lateral subluxation of the patella and signs of impingement of the patellar tendon on the lateral femoral condyle with edema in the parapatellar fat pad.
Intra-articularly, there is a fluid collection with the presence of small loose bodies in the lateral parapatellar recess.

CONCLUSION:
1. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the patellofemoral joint.
2. Joint effusion and small loose bodies with features of early chondromatosis secondary to osteoarthritis.
3. The cystic lesions in the tibial epiphysis could represent either confluent small intraosseous ganglion cysts or subarticular degenerative cysts.
4. Findings of impingement syndrome of the lateral patellar tendon on the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle.

Findings: The lateral meniscus is normal. Grade II degeneration is observed in the horn and body segment of the medial meniscus. There is also a radial tear at the posterior horn level. Cartilage thinning on the medial facet of the patella, and subchondral edema and cartilage thinning on the lateral facet are observed. Signal change consistent with tendinosis is observed at the proximal insertion level of the medial crus of the gastrocnemius. Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint, subchondral sclerosis and edema in the medial tibial plateau adjacent to the joint are observed. Thinning and focal destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilages are observed at this level. A 1 cm diameter ganglion cyst is observed in the extra-articular space of the popliteal fossa.

Suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint, grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Grade II chondromalacia of the medial and lateral facets of the patella. The examination was performed on a 3 Tesla scanner using T2 and PD pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
RIGHT KNEE

1. A partial tear is observed in the medial patellar retinaculum (medial patellofemoral ligament).
2. Subtotal tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
3. Degeneration and tear are observed in the posterior inferior portion of the medial meniscus.
4. Hemarthrosis-hydroarthrosis is observed in communication with a Baker's synovial cyst of maximum diameter 6 cm in the medial popliteal fossa.
6. Ganglion cysts measuring 12 and 15 mm are identified posterior to the medial meniscus and the posterior cruciate ligament.
7. Anterior to the anterior cruciate ligament, a ligament (anteromedial meniscofemoral ligament) is identified as an anatomical variant, with findings of tear at its femoral attachment.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS

From evaluation of the medial compartment, degeneration and subluxation of the meniscus are observed, with focal thinning of the articular cartilage (ICRS grade III) and presence of marginal osteophytes. The findings are consistent with moderate-severity degenerative osteoarthritis.

In the lateral compartment, mild degenerative osteoarthritis is observed with presence of marginal osteophytes and meniscal degeneration, but without significant thinning or erosion of the articular cartilage.

From evaluation of the anterior (patellofemoral) compartment, marginal osteophytes are observed on the patella and trochlea, with degeneration of the articular cartilage at the central portion of the articular surface of the patella and presence of a deep detachment of the articular cartilage measuring 4.5 mm in width (delamination).

Intra-articularly, a joint effusion is observed in communication with a small Baker's cyst, which demonstrates focal synovitis, as well as presence of multiple cartilaginous loose bodies (synovial chondromatosis).

In the superior medial portion of Hoffa's fat pad, edema is observed representing mild impingement syndrome.

Small ganglion cysts are observed posterior to the joint capsule.

ACL.evidence: The ACL is not mentioned anywhere in the report. The overall context is chronic degenerative disease without any traumatic mechanism, making an ACL tear unlikely but not explicitly excluded.

MCL.evidence: The MCL is not mentioned. No ligamentous injury is described; the report focuses entirely on degenerative changes.

Medial Meniscus.evidence: "degeneration and subluxation of the meniscus are observed" – degeneration and subluxation (extrusion) are described, but no discrete tear reaching the articular surface is stated. In the setting of moderate OA a degenerative tear is plausible but not confirmed by the text.

Lateral Meniscus.evidence: "meniscal degeneration, but without significant thinning or erosion of the articular cartilage" – only degenerative signal is noted; no tear is described.

Medial OA.evidence: "focal thinning of the articular cartilage (ICRS grade III) and presence of marginal osteophytes. The findings are consistent with moderate-severity degenerative osteoarthritis." ICRS grade III qualifies as substantial cartilage loss per the panel definition.

Lateral OA.evidence: "mild degenerative osteoarthritis is observed with presence of marginal osteophytes and meniscal degeneration, but without significant thinning or erosion of the articular cartilage." Marginal osteophytes alone without meaningful cartilage loss → ~0.3.

PF OA.evidence: "marginal osteophytes are observed on the patella and trochlea, with degeneration of the articular cartilage at the central portion of the articular surface of the patella and presence of a deep detachment of the articular cartilage measuring 4.5 mm in width (delamination)." Deep delamination represents grade 3–4 chondropathy of the patellofemoral compartment.

Effusion.evidence: "a joint effusion is observed in communication with a small Baker's cyst" – unqualified 'joint effusion' without a size modifier maps to moderate per the calibration rules.

Synovitis.evidence: "focal synovitis" is explicitly stated within the Baker's cyst; additionally, "edema…representing mild impingement syndrome" in Hoffa's fat pad (hoffitis) and "multiple cartilaginous loose bodies (synovial chondromatosis)" indicate synovial involvement.

Baker's.evidence: "a small Baker's cyst, which demonstrates focal synovitis" – explicitly identified.

Contusion.evidence: No bone bruise, marrow oedema of traumatic origin, or muscle contusion is described. The Hoffa's fat pad oedema is attributed to impingement, not trauma. The entire presentation is degenerative.

Fracture.evidence: No fracture, insufficiency fracture, or avulsion is mentioned. The cartilaginous delamination is a chondral lesion, not a bony fracture.

text: MRI findings: The bones forming the left knee joint are of normal shape, structure, and signal intensity. No evidence of joint effusion. The articular cartilage of the tibia and femur is preserved. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus is torn. Along the entire length of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, a thick hyperintense lesion with oblique course is seen, reaching the edge of the meniscus. Medial to the meniscus, a large multiloculated cystic lesion is seen, which is associated with the torn medial meniscus. The cyst measures approximately 44/26 mm in overall size. Lateral meniscus and anterior horn of the medial meniscus – unremarkable. Anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments – normal appearance. At the distal end of the patellar ligament, a rounded bony structure measuring 11 mm is seen. The shape of the tibial tuberosity is altered with a bony defect. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Retinacula – unremarkable. Patellar cartilage, patella – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon – unremarkable. No changes are seen in the soft tissues of the left knee. Conclusion: MRI findings of injury to the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 3 with meniscal cyst. The changes at the caudal end of the patellar ligament and at the tibial tuberosity may be associated with unresolved Osgood-Schlatter disease or an old avulsion injury with ossification formation within the patellar ligament.

MRI findings: MRI evidence of joint effusion. Osteophytes have formed along the medial and lateral articular margins of the femur and tibia, as well as along the anterior surface of the medial femoral condyle. MRI evidence of limited bone marrow edema in the region of the medial femoral condyle, as well as subchondrally in the medial tibial plateau. Presence of small subchondrally located cysts in the medial femoral condyle and in the patella. The articular cartilage of the tibia and femur on the medial half of the joint is thinned, in places lysed, to a greater degree on the femoral side. The patellar cartilage is of preserved thickness. MRI evidence of damage to the medial meniscus. In the anterior horn of the medial meniscus, a hyperintense line with a horizontal course is seen, which reaches the edge of the meniscus and extends into the body and to its posterior horn. Degenerative changes are depicted in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, in which a triangular zone of increased signal intensity is seen ("meniscus-within-meniscus sign"). Both menisci are extruded laterally, without fragment formation. MRI evidence of partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. The fibers of the posterolateral bundle of the ligament are of wider cross-section and with increased signal intensity. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Patellar retinacula – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon, patellar ligament – with preserved thickness and signal characteristics. A small perisynovial cyst is seen, located dorsally, measuring 8.7/5.0 mm. A small multilocular Baker's cyst with typical location and dimensions of 13/8 mm. MRI evidence of subcutaneous edema along the anterolateral and, to a lesser degree, along the anteromedial surface of the knee joint and lower leg. Soft tissue edema around the medial collateral ligament.

Conclusion: MRI evidence of joint effusion. Medial gonarthrosis – grade II–III. Bone marrow edema with the described location. Degenerative damage in the anterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2b; damage in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus – grade 2c. Partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Perisynovial cyst. Multilocular Baker's cyst. Soft tissue and subcutaneous edema.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

MRI LEFT KNEE

Technique: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

Findings:
- From the evaluation of the medial compartment, destruction of the articular cartilage is identified (mostly ICRS grade 4) with degeneration and subluxation of the medial meniscus and large marginal osteophytes. A large complex of parameniscal cysts arises from the body of the medial meniscus and extends posteriorly to the medial collateral ligament with maximum dimensions 3.4 x 2 x 3 cm (transverse x anteroposterior x craniocaudal).
- From the evaluation of the lateral compartment, degeneration of the lateral meniscus is identified, thinning of the articular cartilage (ICRS up to grade 3) and marginal osteophytes. The popliteus tendon also shows degeneration.
- From the evaluation of the patellofemoral joint, thinning and focal loss of the articular cartilage is observed (ICRS up to grade 4) as well as marginal osteophytes on the femoral trochlea and the superior pole of the patella.
- Osteophytes are also observed within the intercondylar notch in combination with a complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
- Joint effusion is observed intra-articularly with the presence of loose bodies.
- Benign hypertrophy is observed in the bone marrow of the tibia and the femur.
- A small Baker's synovial cyst is seen adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle.

CONCLUSION
- Degenerative osteoarthritis in all compartments of the knee, particularly pronounced in the medial compartment.
- Large parameniscal cyst from the medial meniscus.
- Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
- Prepatellar bursitis.

MRI findings: No MRI evidence of joint effusion. The bones forming the right knee joint are of normal shape. A limited zone of bone marrow edema is seen in the medial tibial condyle. MRI evidence of an oval bone lesion located centrally in the proximal tibial diaphysis. The finding measures 6/5 mm and has typical macromorphology of an enchondroma.
The articular cartilage of the tibia and femur has preserved thickness and congruence. MRI evidence of damage in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. A hyperintense line with horizontal course is seen within it, reaching the meniscal edge without contact with the articular surfaces of the tibia and femur. MRI evidence of degenerative changes and damage in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. The posterior horn of the lateral meniscus shows diffusely increased signal intensity, with a hyperintense line of horizontal course also seen within it. The line does not reach the articular surfaces of the bones. Normal appearance of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus and the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. MRI evidence of partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. It is thickened and with diffusely increased signal intensity. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. MRI evidence of total rupture of the medial collateral ligament. The ligament is traced with preserved integrity and signal intensity only in its proximal part at its femoral attachment. In its middle third it shows increased signal intensity, and distally it does not attach to the tibia. Lateral collateral ligament – unremarkable. MRI evidence of a small zone of increased signal intensity in the semimembranosus tendon. This zone is located at the insertion site of the tendon on the medial tibial condyle. Patella, patellar cartilage – unremarkable. Patellar retinacula – normal appearance. Patellar ligament and quadriceps femoris tendon – normal appearance. Popliteal fossa – unremarkable. MRI evidence of edema in the soft tissues on the medial side of the joint, as well as in the subcutaneous tissue of the anterior surface of the lower leg.
Conclusion: MRI evidence of partial rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament – grade 2. Damage in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2a. Degenerative changes and damage in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus – grade 2c. Rupture of the medial collateral ligament. Limited zone of bone marrow edema in the medial tibial condyle. Soft tissue and subcutaneous edema. Tendinopathy at the insertion site of the semimembranosus muscle on the tibia. Enchondroma in the tibial diaphysis.

MRI LEFT KNEE

INDICATION:? Meniscal injury

Routine MRI of the left knee shows a tiny hairline superior surfacing tear in the body of the medial meniscus. There is linear degenerative signal in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus but no discrete tear. ACL and PCL are intact. Extensor mechanism intact. Slight ossification distal quads tendon. No knee joint effusion. Tiny Baker's cyst. Slight fluid is seen in the popliteal fossa between the medial gastrocs and popliteus measuring 5 mm in thickness by 25 mm in width by 42 mm in length. I question the possibility of previous plantaris rupture.

Tricompartmental osteophytes consistent with osteoarthritis. Focal severe chondrosis along the posterior weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle where there is underlying 8 mm focus of bony edema. Severe cartilage loss in the patella with no underlying bone marrow edema.

Tiny hairline superior surfacing tear in the body of the medial meniscus. Degenerative signal in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus with no discrete tear.

Tricompartmental degenerative changes with 8 mm focus of bony edema in the medial femoral condyle and severe cartilage denuding throughout the patella.

Complex fluid is seen in the proximal calf, the inferior aspect is not included on this study suspicious for plantaris rupture.

INDICATION:    Three-month history of nontraumatic left posterior knee pain. Ultrasound suggests medial meniscal tear. Assess for internal derangement   .

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

There is splitting of the fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament unassociated with thickening or deficiency. The finding is favored to represent a described but rare anatomic variant. The lateral patellofemoral ligament is intact and unremarkable.

Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint appears to be reasonably well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

The medial meniscus is intact. Involving the posterior horn and posterior body of medial meniscus there is some contour flattening of the inferior margin of the meniscus peripherally suggesting possible deficiency of a portion of the meniscotibial ligamentous attachment. There is no evidence of a significant medial meniscal tear. Articular cartilage of the medial compartment is reasonably well-maintained. There is fraying seen to the posterior surface of the weightbearing surface of medial femoral condyle consistent with moderate focal chondrosis.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact. Fibers appear mildly attenuated compatible with a remote partial-thickness sprain. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Projecting in the intercondylar notch surrounding the anterior cruciate ligament, situated anterior to the posterior cruciate ligament there is a multiloculated ganglion cyst measuring about 1.9 cm in length and 1.5 x 1.3 cm in short axis. The finding is consistent with an anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst.

The medial collateral ligament is intact.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is no evidence of a significant Baker's cyst. A small 8 x 4 mm ganglion cyst is seen projecting posterior to the proximal tendon fibers of the medial head of the gastrocnemius.

Marrow signal is within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Moderate chondrosis to the medial joint compartment associated with contour flattening of the inferior surface of the posterior horn and posterior body of medial meniscus. This finding is equivocal but could indicate presence of partial deficiency of the meniscotibial attachment in this region. No discrete medial meniscal tear is identified.

Mild attenuation of the anterior cruciate ligament consistent with remote partial thickness injury. Associated anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst.

Suspected congenital duplication of the medial patellar retinaculum.

text: Tricompartmental degenerative joint disease of the knee, most prominent in the medial femorotibial compartment, characterized by full-thickness articular cartilage loss and degeneration, subchondral medullary fibrocystic and fibrovascular changes, and marginal osteophytes. A loose body measuring 5 mm in diameter is located in the vicinity of the anterior root of the medial meniscus. A loose body measuring 5 mm in diameter is located between the posterior cruciate ligament and the joint capsule. The intra-articular fluid volume in the knee joint is mildly increased. The cruciate and collateral ligaments are normal. Degeneration at the body of the lateral meniscus is accompanied by a horizontal oblique tear involving the inferior articular surface, with a defect at the free edge. The medial meniscus is extruded medially by 7 mm. Irregularity of the superior and inferior articular surfaces of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus suggests a complex degenerative tear extending to both the superior and inferior articular surfaces. A 5 mm diameter intraosseous ganglion cyst at the tibial insertion of the posterior cruciate ligament is surrounded by mild edema. The extensor mechanism is intact.

PF OA.evidence: Tricompartmental degenerative joint disease of the knee, most prominent in the medial femorotibial compartment, characterized by full-thickness articular cartilage loss and degeneration, subchondral medullary fibrocystic and fibrovascular changes, and marginal osteophytes.

Synovitis.evidence: Tricompartmental degenerative joint disease of the knee, most prominent in the medial femorotibial compartment, characterized by full-thickness articular cartilage loss and degeneration, subchondral medullary fibrocystic and fibrovascular changes, and marginal osteophytes.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 6 months of atraumatic knee pain, no prior surgeries
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Areas of high-grade partial thickness cartilage loss in the central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness chondrosis in the central weightbearing aspect of the lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full thickness cartilage loss in the lateral patellar facet and median ridge with subchondral marrow edema. Additional high-grade partial thickness loss across the medial patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Lateral patellar tilt and translation. Patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Top normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 16 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Tricompartmental osteoarthritis most prominent in the patellofemoral compartment.

2. Chronic superolateral patellofemoral maltracking.

Interpretation:

There is a minimal amount of fluid in the suprapatellar recess, which could be physiological in nature or related to a minimal joint effusion. There is no Baker's cyst.

The medial meniscus as well as the medial collateral ligament are intact and without tear. There is minimal attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment, without full-thickness defect or reactive subchondral change.

The lateral meniscus as well as the lateral collateral ligament complex are intact and without tear. The lateral femorotibial compartment is preserved, without full-thickness defect or reactive subchondral change.

The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact and without tear.

Patellofemoral alignment is within normal limits.

Small knee joint effusion. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

Subtle peripheral bone edema of the medial tibial plateau at the insertion site of the deep meniscofemoral ligament of the medial complex, which could represent a non-displaced avulsive injury.

text: RIGHT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: The lateral meniscus is normal. The medial meniscus is extruded 3.5 mm medially from the knee joint. Volume loss is present in the meniscus, with grade III degeneration observed in the posterior horn and body segments. Loss of continuity secondary to complete rupture is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. No joint effusion is detected. A well-defined, subcortically located lesion measuring 31x15 mm in the posterior aspect of the distal femoral metaphysis, slightly hypointense on T1 and T2-weighted images with a T2 hyperintense central area, of benign morphology not causing cortical destruction, was observed. The described lesion was primarily interpreted as a non-ossifying fibroma. Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral compartment, subchondral sclerosis and irregularity on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint, and subchondral millimetric cysts and edema in the medial femoral condyle were observed. Loss of integrity in the femoral and tibial cartilages at this level was observed. Findings were interpreted as degenerative arthritis. CONCLUSION: Non-ossifying fibroma of the femur, gonarthrosis, volume loss and medial extrusion of the medial meniscus, complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and STIR. A T2 gradient echo sequence was also acquired. [DATE].

FINDINGS:
Re-evaluation of the complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
Re-evaluation of the partial injury of the upper third of the posterior cruciate ligament, showing improvement in imaging characteristics.
The foci of bone bruise that had been observed in the region of the distal femur and proximal tibia are no longer observed.
Callus formation of the fracture of the fibular head is observed with mild alteration of the superior surface (malunion).
In the lateral femoral condyle, a small bone infarct is observed, probably secondary to a previous bone bruise in the area.
In the medial femoral condyle, a small subarticular insufficiency fracture is observed (synonymous with "spontaneous osteonecrosis") with extensive bone edema. Bone densitometry of the lumbar spine is recommended.
The articular surfaces are evaluated as intact.
Mild tendinopathy is observed in the superior portion of the patellar tendon.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T2, T2 me2d, and PD FS sequences.

FINDINGS:
- Blurring of the proximal fibers of both cruciate ligaments is noted, in the context of complete tears. The probability of a few intact fibers is considered low.
- Diffuse pathological signal with accompanying blurring of the proximal insertion of the lateral collateral ligament is recognized, in the context of a partial tear, while there is coexisting morphological thinning at its midportion, possibly in the context of a morphological tear.
- Numerous areas of pathological bone marrow signal are observed in both the femoral and tibial condyles, in the context of residual bone edema. A microtrabecular fracture is noted in the lateral femoral condyle subarticularly, with a transverse dimension of ~8.5 mm.
- An avulsion fracture of the fibular head is noted with displacement up to 5 mm.
- Intense edema of the periarticular soft tissues is observed, mainly at the medial aspect, in the popliteal fossa and at the level of the gastrocnemius muscles, in the context of both the aforementioned injury as well as other postoperative procedures.
- Thickening and pathological signal are observed in the popliteus tendon.
- The menisci and articular cartilage are satisfactorily evaluated.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: No meniscal tear or extrusion. Mild intrasubstance degeneration of the posterior horn.
Medial compartment cartilage: Mild loss of cartilage along the weightbearing aspect of the mediofemoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:

Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild loss of cartilage along the lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Small partial-thickness cartilage defect along the lateral patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Increased tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 19 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Imaged tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear. There is mild edema deep to the sartorius and gracilis tendons at the level of the knee joint which may represent bursitis.

IMPRESSION:

text:
MRI of Left Knee with 
-SG PD FatSat, Locator, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

* Shallow trochlear groove with supratrochlear spur and lateral displacement of patella, indicative of trochlear dysplasia with suspicious of lateral patellar tilting.
   Increased signal intensity of the medial and lateral patellar retinaculum with surrounding soft tissue edema, in favor of grade 2 injury.
   Bone marrow edema over medial aspect of patella and lateral aspect of lateral femoral condyle, R/O bone contusion.
* Wearing of the articular cartilage of patellofemoral joint and spur formation of patella, femur and anterior tibial plateau with subchondral bone marrow edema, reflecting osteoarthritis; subchondral cystic change over tibial plateau.
* There is linear signal intensity in anterior horn of lateral meniscus and posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extends into the surface, R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal, maybe due to degeneration.
* High signal intensity in the soft tissues around the medial and lateral collateral ligaments and ACL, in favor of grade 1 injury.
* Joint effusion with suprapatellar expension and hypertrophy of the synovium; suprapatellar, medial and lateral plicae can also be noted, indicative of synovitis.
* Subcutaneous edema around left knee; increased fat stranding over infrapatellar fat pad.
* Mild muscle edema over vastus medialis muscle.
> The contour of PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> No evidence of tear is noted in  lateral meniscus in this study.
> The quadriceps and patellar tendons appear to be within normal.

Impression:
1. Transient patellar dislocation with tear of medial patellar retinaculum near patellar attachment and bone contusion of medial aspect of patella and lateral femoral condyle.
2. Trochlear dysplasia with shallow femoral trochlear groove and in favor of lateral patellar tilting in this study.
3. Grade 1 injury of ACL, MCL and  LCL.
4. Subcutaneous and interstitial edema around left knee and muscle edema over vastus medialis muscle.
5. Osteoarthritis of left knee with synovitis and patellar plicae.
6. R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal in anterior horn of lateral meniscus and posterior horn of medial meniscus.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

Interpretation:

There is no intra-articular effusion nor significant Baker's cyst with a rim of fluid.

There is a multilobulated cystic formation at the posteromedial aspect of the knee extending to both the semimembranosus bursa and the posterior intercondylar region, measuring approximately 0.9 x 4.2 x 2.1 cm in AP, transverse, and CC diameter. There is vertical blunting at the periphery of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, of lower signal compared to fluid, which could be related to an old vertical longitudinal tear at the capsulomeniscal junction/ramp lesion. This cystic formation could be related to a parameniscal cyst in this context or a paraganglionic cyst.

There is slight diffuse attenuation of the chondral surfaces at the medial femorotibial compartment, without full-thickness defect nor associated reactive subchondral change, except for minimal subchondral edema at the tibial side.

There is slight diffuse attenuation of the chondral surfaces at the patellofemoral compartment, without full-thickness defect.

There is a small enthesophyte at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon with minimal associated reactive edema. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact and without tear. There is no significant prepatellar or infrapatellar bursitis noted.

Conclusion:

There is slight vertical blunting at the periphery of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus which could be related to an old vertical longitudinal tear at the capsulomeniscal junction/ramp lesion. There is slight patellofemoral and medial femorotibial chondropathy.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1-weighted, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
The following were observed:

1. Meniscocapsular detachment is identified in the lateral meniscus with tear of the posterior superior popliteomeniscal fascicle and the meniscofemoral ligament.

2. A bucket handle tear is observed in the medial meniscus with displacement of meniscal material into the intercondylar notch.

3. Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

4. Complete tear of the posterior cruciate ligament with an old avulsion fracture, callused, at its insertion on the posterior surface of the tibia.

5. Edematous signal of the tibialis anterior muscle is observed, as in injury of the deep peroneal nerve.

6. Bone bruise is observed in a resolving phase (compared to the previous examination), at the medial femoral and medial tibial condyle.

7. Small loose bodies are observed intra-articularly.

8. Thinning of the articular cartilage of the lateral femoral and lateral tibial condyle is present from the previous injury.

9. Posterior to the torn posterior cruciate ligament, a ganglion cyst measuring 22x18x9 mm is identified.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo, and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
In the lateral compartment, no significant pathological findings are observed.
In the medial compartment, there is a degenerative tear of the medial meniscus and extrusion of the remaining meniscal material, full-thickness erosion of the articular cartilage of both the femoral condyle and the tibia over an anteroposterior diameter of at least 12 mm, mild bone marrow edema in the medial femoral condyle, and more extensive bone marrow edema in the medial tibial condyle where a low-signal area is also demonstrated on all pulse sequences, measuring 6 mm in anteroposterior diameter.
Intra-articularly, a large joint effusion is observed with focal frond-like projections of fatty composition and the presence of a large synovial fold suprapatellarly.
The ligamentous structures are intact.
A small enchondroma measuring 5 mm, of no clinical significance, is observed in the central portion of the tibial metaphysis.

CONCLUSION:
1. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the medial compartment.
2. Trabecular insufficiency microfracture of the medial tibial condyle (synonymous with "spontaneous osteonecrosis").
3. Hydrarthrosis with small-scale development of secondary frond-like lipoma (lipoma arborescens).

1. Moderate to severe degenerative changes most pronounced medially.

2. Diffuse intrasubstance degeneration with maceration, extrusion and degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus. Intrasubstance degeneration of the lateral meniscus without tear.

3. Intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the ACL without ligament injury.

text: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: The medial meniscus is extruded 5.5 mm medially from the knee joint. Volume loss is noted in the meniscus, with grade III degeneration in the posterior horn and body segment and an accompanying horizontal tear. Grade III degeneration is observed in the anterior horn, posterior horn, and body segment of the lateral meniscus. Loss of integrity secondary to complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament is observed. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. A 2x1 cm loculated fluid collection is observed in the prepatellar subcutaneous fat tissue with accompanying diffuse edema in the subcutaneous fat tissue. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Joint space narrowing is observed in the medial tibiofemoral compartment with subchondral sclerosis, edema, and degenerative cysts on the articular bone surfaces adjacent to the joint. Cartilage destruction is observed in the femoral and tibial cartilages at this level. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis. Subchondral degenerative cysts are observed in the tibial intercondylar eminence. Mild fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa. Fluid increase is observed in the pes anserine bursa. Central-marginal osteophyte formation is observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis, medial extrusion of the medial meniscus, volume loss and grade III meniscopathy of the medial meniscus, grade III meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus, complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament, grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament, prepatellar bursitis, pes anserine bursitis, suprapatellar bursitis.

- Full-thickness cartilage defects and thinning of the articular cartilage are observed in the medial compartment of the knee. There is coexisting subchondral bone marrow edema of the tibia and marginal osteophytes. The articular surfaces of the anterior and lateral compartments are within normal limits.
- A degenerative tear is observed in the body of the medial meniscus with associated subluxation. The lateral meniscus is normal.
- A small intra-articular fluid collection is observed in the knee joint.
- On evaluation of the cruciate and collateral ligaments, the extensor mechanism, and the bone marrow, no pathological findings are observed.
- An accessory fabella is identified posterior to the lateral femoral condyle as an anatomical variant.

text: RIGHT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Central-marginal osteophyte formation was observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint, subchondral sclerosis, edema, and degenerative millimetric cysts were observed on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint. Cartilage destruction was observed in the femoral and tibial cartilages at this level. Findings were interpreted as degenerative arthritis. The medial meniscus is completely extruded 6 mm medially from the knee joint. Decrease in meniscal volume, grade III degeneration, and complex tears are observed in the meniscus. The lateral meniscus is extruded 5 mm laterally from the knee joint space. Loss of integrity was observed in the posterior horn and body of the meniscus. Grade III degeneration is observed in the anterior horn. The anterior cruciate ligament is markedly thinned and shows increased signal on PD images. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Periligamentous edema was observed in the medial collateral ligament. Periarticular loose body formations, the largest measuring 7 mm in diameter, were observed in the lateral tibiofemoral joint. The tibiofibular joint space is narrowed, and subchondral cysts were observed in the lateral tibial plateau and fibular head adjacent to the joint. A Baker's cyst measuring 7x2 cm was observed in the popliteal fossa. Edema is observed in the prepatellar subcutaneous fat tissue. Fluid increase was observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Conclusion: Gonarthrosis. Extrusion from the joint space, volume loss, grade III degeneration, and complex tears in the medial and lateral menisci. Near-complete large tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Suprapatellar bursitis. Synovitis of the knee joint. Arthrosis of the tibiofibular joint. Periarticular loose body formations in the anterior tibiofemoral joint. Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa. Subchondral bone marrow edema in the patella.

The anterior horn is anteriorly extruded. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is reasonably well-maintained with mild fraying seen at the weightbearing surface in keeping with moderate chondrosis.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex are all intact.

No significant Baker's cyst is demonstrated.

There is a large knee effusion demonstrated.

There is edema and soft tissue stranding in the popliteal fossa

Bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus associated with moderate articular chondrosis to the articular cartilage of the medial femoral condyle. Associated meniscal/parameniscal cyst arising at the posterior root of medial meniscus.

Large knee effusion.

Interpretation:

There is a small but significant intra-articular effusion. There is no Baker's cyst.

The medial meniscus is intact and without tear.

There is mild thickening of the medial collateral ligament involving, in particular, the proximal superficial fibers, associated with mild surrounding edema, consistent with a grade 1 sprain. There is a small area of edema at the posteromedial aspect of the medial femoral condyle suggesting a small associated bone contusion.

There is mild diffuse attenuation of the cartilage surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment with a high-grade, full-thickness chondral fissure at the junction of the weight-bearing and non-weight-bearing surfaces of the medial femoral condyle, associated with reactive subchondral changes.

There is a small oblique tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. There is no displaced meniscal fragment.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact and without tear.

There is moderate attenuation of the cartilage surfaces in the lateral femorotibial compartment with a full-thickness chondral fissure on the femoral side and associated reactive subchondral changes.

Additionally, there is a subchondral trabecular impaction fracture at the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau with significant associated bone edema extending anteriorly and medially. There is no associated depression of the cartilage surface.

There is thickening and more marked increased signal of the anterior cruciate ligament at its mid and proximal portions, suggesting an intermediate-grade sprain/partial tear. There is also a mild low-grade interstitial longitudinal delamination/tear of the mid and proximal fibers of the posterior cruciate ligament. There is no evidence of full-thickness involvement of the cruciate ligaments.

Patellofemoral alignment is preserved. There is mild to moderate attenuation of the patellofemoral cartilage surfaces with a full-thickness chondral fissure at the junction of the patellar apex and the lateral patellar facet, as well as along the lateral trochlea, with a focus of associated reactive subchondral changes.

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact and without tear.

Conclusion:

There is a subchondral trabecular impaction fracture at the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau, without depression of the articular surface. There is significant associated bone edema as detailed above.

There is a grade 1 sprain of the medial collateral ligament with a small associated bone contusion at the medial femoral condyle.

There is an intermediate-grade sprain/partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is a low-grade interstitial longitudinal delamination/tear of the posterior cruciate ligament. There is no full-thickness involvement of the cruciate ligaments.

There is a small oblique tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. There is no displaced meniscal fragment.

There is no patellar fracture.

The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

The findings are in the differential diagnosis between inflammatory arthritis and early lipoma arborescens.
Rheumatological evaluation is recommended.

Findings:

There is a moderate joint effusion with signs of synovitis.

There is no popliteal cyst.

The patella is positioned slightly high (patella alta). In addition, there is a mild lateral tilt of the patella, without evidence of subluxation.

There is mild patellar tendinopathy. There is no bursitis, but there is edema anterior to the patellar tendon extending down to the tibial tuberosity. The medial patellar retinaculum is slightly irregular. Hoffa's fat pad is normal. The suprapatellar fat pad is also normal.

There is grade 2 to 3 chondrosis of the patellofemoral cartilage.

There is a chronic tear of the medial meniscus. It involves the root of the posterior horn, which demonstrates increased signal with signs of maceration. This explains the significant extrusion of the body of the medial meniscus with intrasubstance edema. There is also mild extrusion of the anterior horn of this meniscus.

The lateral meniscus does not demonstrate any significant abnormality.

The anterior cruciate ligament does not demonstrate a tear.

The posterior cruciate ligament is normal.

The lateral ligamentous complex does not demonstrate any significant abnormality.

The medial collateral ligament is bowed due to the extrusion of the medial meniscus. It is also slightly thickened at its superior portion, consistent with a chronic sprain. There is no tear.

There is bone marrow edema at the corner of the medial tibial plateau in relation to this medial meniscus tear. There is also grade 2 to 3 chondrosis of the medial tibiofemoral compartment with joint space narrowing.

The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.

Conclusion:

The main abnormality is this chronic tear of the medial meniscus. Since the root of the posterior horn is torn, there is complete extrusion of the body and mild extrusion of the anterior horn. This means that the meniscus no longer serves its function. Furthermore, there is joint space narrowing of the medial compartment with grade 2 to 3 chondrosis. There are also stress changes at the periphery of the medial tibial plateau as described above. This can obviously cause pain with walking and in the standing position. Clinical correlation is recommended.

MRI Findings: Post-traumatic condition. The bones forming the knee joint are of normal shape and structure. Their signal characteristics are altered as a result of massive bone marrow edema in the tibial epiphysis and the lateral condyles of the femur and tibia. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia is preserved. Joint effusion is present. MRI evidence of complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. It shows increased signal intensity and enlarged diameter, and is not visualized at its typical location. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact, with preserved continuity. The posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is not visualized at its anatomic location. It is displaced medially into the joint and is partially located beneath the lateral intercondylar eminence. The Double PCL sign is present – pathognomonic for a bucket-handle lesion of the lateral meniscus. Normal appearance of the medial meniscus in both its horns. No evidence of traumatic changes of the collateral ligaments. Patella, patellar cartilage, retinacula – normal appearance. Patellar ligament, quadriceps femoris tendon – unremarkable. No pathological changes are found in the popliteal fossa and intercondylar fossa. No post-traumatic soft tissue edema.

Conclusion: MRI evidence of complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. The described lesion in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is of bucket-handle type. Post-traumatic bone marrow edema.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Medial meniscus injury; 5 months of left knee pain, initially 
improved and now persistent for 2 months after fall down the stairs. Inner 
knee pain 
Comparison: Left knee radiographs [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated 
knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard 
non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow 
signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive 
osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate, partially 
ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Peripheral vertical tear of the posterior horn extending 
to the body.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Areas of full-thickness cartilage 
loss along the medial facet and median ridge as well as central trochlea 
with underlying subchondral edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete tear of the midportion of the 
ACL.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Grade 2 sprain of the 
popliteofibular ligament. Periligamentous edema about the lateral 
collateral ligament with intact fibers.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. Ganglion cyst of the popliteus 
tendon sheath.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No 
lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and 
trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) 
distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not 
previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. 
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Venous 
fluid-fluid level in the popliteal fossa. 

IMPRESSION:
1.  Complete tear of the ACL with moderate joint effusion.
2.  Peripheral vertical tear (RAMP lesion) of the posterior horn extending 
to the body of the medial meniscus.
3.  Grade 2 sprain of the popliteofibular ligament and grade 1 strain of the distal lateral collateral ligament. Correlate for posterolateral corner instability.

MRI KNEE

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo sequences.

FINDINGS:
- On evaluation of the medial compartment, significant degenerative osteoarthritis is observed with full-thickness erosion of the articular cartilage of the medial femoral and tibial condyles (ICRS IV), presence of marginal osteophytes and subarticular osteomyelitis edema, and degenerative tear and displacement of the medial meniscus.
- On evaluation of the lateral compartment, small marginal osteophytes, mild superficial cartilage erosion, and mild meniscal degeneration are observed.
- On evaluation of the anterior (patellofemoral) compartment, moderate degeneration of the articular cartilage on the lateral articular surface and an osteophyte on the medial articular surface of the patella are identified.
- The medial meniscus correspondingly presents with extrusion and degenerative tear of its posterior horn.
- On evaluation of the ligaments, mucoid degeneration and partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament are noted, most likely due to impingement from an osteophyte formation arising from the medial margin of the lateral femoral condyle, in the intercondylar notch.
- Moderate intra-articular fluid collection is observed.
- A large Baker's cyst measuring 9.2 cm x 5.9 cm x 3.8 cm is noted at the site of the palpable mass (clinical question).
- Small cyst in the mid-portion of the tibial plateau, of no clinical significance.

The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

Degenerative changes of the medial compartment with persistence of subchondral bone marrow edema in the medial tibial condyle, in only slightly lesser extent. Degenerative tendinopathy of the semimembranosus tendon. Significant intra-articular fluid collection.

LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of both the medial and lateral meniscus. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Loss of integrity secondary to complete rupture is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Thinning and periligamentous edema are observed in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. A subarticular nondisplaced fracture and edema in the adjacent bone marrow are observed in the lateral femoral condyle. Contusional bone marrow edema is observed in the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau and in the fibular head. Mild anterior subluxation of the tibia at the tibiofemoral joint is observed. Signal increase due to edema on STIR sequence in the muscle tissue at the proximal portion of the soleus muscle, and increased fluid at the muscle belly is present.
CONCLUSION: Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. Kissing contusion in the tibia and femur and subarticular fracture in the femur. Mild anterior subluxation of the tibia. Grade II meniscopathy in the medial and lateral meniscus. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Suprapatellar bursitis, mild synovitis of the knee joint. Grade I strain of the soleus muscle.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, T2, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
Intra-articularly, there is a significant joint effusion. The medial meniscus shows abnormal signal at its posterior horn, with displacement of a meniscal fragment into the intercondylar notch. Also, a displaced fragment is observed at its anterior horn. The lateral meniscus, the posterior cruciate ligament, and the lateral collateral ligament appear within normal limits. The medial collateral ligament shows edema around it. The anterior cruciate ligament shows edema and high-grade discontinuity at its proximal portion. Fluid collection is observed prepatellarly. The articular cartilage has normal appearance.

CONCLUSION:

The examination was performed with T1-weighted, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences. [DATE].

6. Bone bruises are re-evaluated at the posterior lateral tibial metaphysis and the anterior lateral femoral condyle, somewhat greater in extent compared to the previous examination (expected finding).

7. The posterior cruciate ligament and the collateral ligaments appear normal.

Between the aforementioned body and the lower pole of the patella and the anterior lateral femoral condyle, edema is observed.

RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
The lateral meniscus is normal. Grade III degeneration and a meniscal root tear are observed in the medial meniscus. The medial meniscus appears extruded medially. Two intra-articular bodies compatible with loose bodies, the larger measuring 6 mm in diameter, are present in the posterior vicinity of the medial meniscus. Periligamentous edema compatible with a grade I sprain is present around the medial collateral ligament. The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, and lateral collateral ligament are normal. The distal quadriceps is normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Osteophytic spurs in the bony structures at the patellofemoral joint level, joint space narrowing, loss of integrity and thinning of the adjacent cartilage, and subchondral bone marrow edema are observed (grade IV chondromalacia). Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and lateral recess. Subchondral millimetric cysts are observed at the intercondylar level of the femur. Several ganglion cysts, the largest measuring 17 mm, are observed in the popliteal fossa. A marked edematous appearance is observed in the subcutaneous fatty tissue at the prepatellar level.

Mild to moderate chondrosis with a focal full-thickness fissure with subchondral bone change at the medial aspect of the lateral patellar facet. Intact extensor mechanism. No significant edema within Hoffa's fat pad.

Moderate chondrosis with area of more than 50% thinning of cartilage. Mild chondrosis. No discrete meniscal tear. Curvilinear bony fragment overlying the posterior aspect of the fibular head most likely related to a prior avulsion injury of arcuate ligament or fabellofibular ligament. Lateral collateral ligament and biceps femoris appear intact. Iliotibial band appears slightly thickened but without surrounding edema, nonspecific.

INTERCONDYLAR COMPARTMENT:
Anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament are intact.

1. Moderate medial compartment chondrosis with complex meniscal tear described above with a flipped fragment medially to the medial tibial plateau and posterior horn flipped fragment near the intercondylar notch.
2. Mild to moderate chondrosis involving the anterior and lateral compartment. Mild synovitis with debris is in the suprapatellar recess.
3. Remote avulsion injury at the proximal medial collateral ligament and fibular head.

Interpretation:

Moderate intra-articular effusion. No significant Baker's cyst.

There is a slightly complex tear of the medial meniscus with a vertical/radial peripheral component of the posterior horn with a possible associated RAMP lesion at the meniscocapsular junction. There is an oblique longitudinal component extending to the junction with the meniscal body. Minimal extrusion of the meniscal body.

There is mild edema surrounding the medial collateral ligament consistent with a grade 1 sprain. There is mild to moderate diffuse attenuation of the cartilage surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment with small marginal osteophytes. There is a minimal focus of edema on the medial aspect of the medial femoral condyle, probably contusive in nature. No full-thickness defect or reactive subchondral change.

Small ganglion cysts at the origin of the gastrocnemii.

The lateral meniscus and the lateral collateral ligament complex are intact without tear. Mild diffuse attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the lateral femorotibial compartment with small marginal osteophytes. No full-thickness defect.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact without tear. There is suspicion of a full-thickness tear, probably of the mid-distal portion of the anterior cruciate ligament, with probably associated contusion on the posterior aspect of the lateral and medial tibial plateaus.

Patellofemoral alignment is preserved.

Small enthesophytes at the distal insertion of the quadriceps with mild tendinosis/enthesopathy. No tear. The patellar tendon is intact without tear.

There is mild to moderate attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the patellofemoral compartment with focal areas of grade 4 chondropathy along the medial patellar facet and the medial trochlea with full-thickness fissures and minimal associated reactive subchondral changes. Small marginal osteophytes.

Conclusion:

Full-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with probably residual associated contusion of the posterior portion of the lateral and medial tibial plateaus.

Complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a vertical/radial peripheral component with a possible associated RAMP lesion at the meniscocapsular junction as well as an oblique longitudinal component extending to the meniscal body.

Diffuse tricompartmental grade 1-2 chondropathy with focal areas of grade 4 chondropathy on the medial aspect of the patellofemoral compartment.

MRI Findings: MRI evidence of a small joint effusion. Normal appearance of the bones forming the right knee joint. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia shows preserved congruence. The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments show preserved integrity and signal characteristics. Suspicious MRI findings for a bucket-handle lesion of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus. The pathognomonic sign is present – double PCL sign, representing a meniscal fragment measuring 7.5/2.5 mm immediately below the cranial third of the posterior cruciate ligament. In the differential diagnosis, it is less likely that the described finding is associated with the posteromedial bundle of the posterior cruciate ligament. The posterior horn is partially ruptured with a grade 2a injury. Degenerative changes in the lateral meniscus. Collateral ligaments – with preserved integrity. Patella, patellar cartilage, retinacula – unremarkable. A ruptured Baker's cyst is visualized at the level of the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle with fluid tracking around the muscle.

Conclusion: Suspicious MRI findings for a bucket-handle lesion of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus. Partial injury of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2a. Early degenerative changes of the lateral meniscus. Ruptured Baker's cyst. Small joint effusion.

Mild to moderate chondromalacia patella.

text:
MRI LEFT KNEE
TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.
FINDINGS
A degenerative tear is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with subluxation thereof.
On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, and the extensor mechanism, no significant findings are observed.
On evaluation of the bone marrow, extensive osteomyelitic edema is observed in the medial metaphysis of the proximal tibia with the presence of a subarticular low signal intensity lesion on all pulse sequences, thin, measuring 12 mm in length.
At the same level, erosion of the articular cartilage ICRS grade III is observed in the medial femoral and medial tibial condyle.
A moderate fluid collection is observed in the knee joint in communication with a Baker's synovial cyst in the medial popliteal fossa.
CONCLUSION
Findings consistent with insufficiency fracture (synonymous with "spontaneous osteonecrosis") in the medial proximal epiphysis of the proximal tibia.
The articular surface is intact.
There is coexisting joint effusion and degenerative tear of the medial meniscus.

- No evidence of extensor mechanism dysfunction is observed.
- An accessory fabella is observed in a typical position posterior to the lateral femoral condyle, as an anatomical variant.

CONCLUSION
1. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the medial compartment with degenerative meniscal tear.
2. Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Joint space narrowing is observed in the medial tibiofemoral joint, with millimetric cyst and edema in the subchondral area of the medial tibial plateau adjacent to the joint. Cartilage destruction is observed in the femoral and tibial cartilages at this level. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis.

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, pd/T2 fs, and T2* pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
- On evaluation of the medial compartment, there is a degenerative complex tear and subluxation of the medial meniscus, full-thickness erosion of the articular cartilage of the medial femoral and tibial condyles (ICRS Grade 4), as well as intense edema of the opposing surfaces of the medial femoral and tibial condyles, consistent with microtrabecular insufficiency fractures. Small marginal osteophytes are also present, one of which projects into the intercondylar notch.
- In the lateral compartment, there is a discoid meniscus which demonstrates a degenerative tear, while there is also folding of a meniscal fragment at the level of the intercondylar notch. The articular cartilage of the lateral femoral condyle shows thinning as well as chondrocalcinosis.
- On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, there is a congenitally shallow trochlea (sulcus angle 165°). Fissural erosions of the articular cartilage of the patella and of the femoral trochlea are also present.
- Intra-articularly, there is a small joint effusion and extensive synovitis with accompanying presence of numerous osteochondral loose bodies measuring 1–2 mm. Additionally, in the lateral aspect of the suprapatellar pouch, there is a projecting synovial formation measuring 1.1 cm with fat signal, which likely represents lipoma arborescens.
- The collateral ligaments and the posterior cruciate ligament appear normal. Myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament.

CONCLUSION:
1) Findings of extensive degenerative osteoarthritis in the medial compartment and early degenerative osteoarthritis in the lateral and anterior compartments.
2) Discoid lateral meniscus with a bucket-handle tear.
3) The findings of intra-articular synovitis and lipoma arborescens are attributed secondarily to degenerative osteoarthritis.
4) The findings from the extensor mechanism are consistent with patellar tracking dysfunction.
