text:
MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

Technique: The examination was performed with T1, PD fs, and T2* pulse sequences.

Findings:
- Presence of a small amount of intra-articular fluid collection.
- There is significant narrowing of the medial compartment joint space, with complete loss of articular cartilage and extensive architectural disruption of the medial meniscus (meniscal maceration). The lateral meniscus shows diffusely increased signal, likely in the context of degeneration.
- Normal appearance of the cruciate and collateral ligaments.
- Bone marrow edema is observed in the lateral tibial condyle, likely in the context of an insufficiency reaction (without clear evidence of fracture) or traumatic origin (correlation with clinical history).
- On evaluation of the patellofemoral joint, architectural disruption of the trochlear cartilage is identified, with thinning and focal defect in the lateral aspect, and correspondingly in the central aspect of the patella, with subchondral cysts at the same level (Grade II and IV respectively).

CONCLUSION: Findings consistent with severe knee osteoarthritis.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

MRI OF THE LEFT KNEE

Technique: The examination was performed with T1, PD fs, and T2* pulse sequences.

Findings:
- Presence of intra-articular fluid collection, predominantly in the medial compartment of the joint, with an accompanying Baker's cyst measuring 6 cm in craniocaudal dimension.
- There is narrowing of the medial compartment joint space, with significant thinning-loss of articular cartilage, severe degeneration of the medial meniscus, architectural disruption and extrusion thereof. A region of bone marrow edema is also observed in the medial femoral condyle, in the subarticular portion of the medial tibial condyle, as well as several subarticular cysts in the posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle. A small bony structure is noted at the medial supracondylar ridge, as in secondary osteochondromatosis.
- Increased signal and thickening of the insertion of the semimembranosus and semitendinosus tendons are observed, in the context of degeneration.
- On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, cruciate ligaments, and collateral ligaments, no significant pathological findings are identified.
- On evaluation of the patellofemoral joint, architectural disruption of the trochlear cartilage is identified, with thinning and focal defect in the lateral aspect, thickness >50% (Grade III).

CONCLUSION: Findings consistent with severe knee osteoarthritis.

- Mild edema is observed in the subcutaneous fat anterior to the patellar tendon, without clinical significance.

CONCLUSION
Degenerative osteoarthritis of the lateral patellofemoral compartment.

LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior and posterior horns and body of the lateral meniscus. Grade III degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Signal change consistent with tendinosis is observed at the proximal insertion level of the medial crus of the gastrocnemius. A 1 cm diameter cyst is observed in the subchondral area of the posterior medial tibial plateau. The distal quadriceps is normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Edema in the subchondral area and significant cartilage thinning are observed at the lateral patellar facet. Increased fluid is observed in the pes anserine bursa. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Joint space narrowing and osteophytic spurring at the corners of the bony structures adjacent to the joint are observed in the medial tibiofemoral joint. Cartilage thinning is observed at the femoral and tibial levels at this level, more pronounced at the tibial level.
CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis. Grade III meniscopathy in the medial meniscus, grade II meniscopathy in the lateral meniscus. Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade II chondromalacia of the lateral patellar facet. Suprapatellar bursitis, pes anserine bursitis. Tendinosis of the medial crus of the gastrocnemius.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
In the lateral compartment of the knee, large marginal osteophytes are observed without significant erosion of the articular cartilage. The lateral meniscus is normal.

In the medial compartment of the knee, severe degenerative osteoarthritis is observed with erosion of the articular cartilage of the femoral and tibial condyle respectively (ICRS grade 4) and accompanying degenerative tear and extrusion of the medial meniscus. Presence of marginal osteophytes as well as multiple ganglion cysts proximal to the joint space with anteroposterior diameter of 2.5 cm and craniocaudal diameter of 2.5 cm.

In the anterior compartment, presence of osteophytosis and mild erosion of the articular cartilage of the patella is noted.

Emphasis is placed on the presence of newly formed bony projections in the intercondylar notch. It is considered likely that the presence of these proliferative structures is responsible for the chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament and the myxoid degeneration of the distal half of the posterior cruciate ligament.

A small joint effusion is observed in the knee joint in communication with a Baker's synovial cyst.

The bone marrow shows benign hyperplasia in the distal femoral metadiaphysis.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

Technique: The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences after application of fat signal suppression.

Findings:
A degenerative tear of the body of the medial meniscus is observed with subluxation of it. In the medial compartment there are coexisting marginal osteophytes and erosion of the articular cartilage in the setting of mild osteoarthritis. On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, the cruciate ligaments and the collateral ligaments, no pathological findings are observed. In the patellofemoral compartment, areas of erosion of the articular cartilage of the patella are identified. Specifically, a superficial tear along the midline (ICRS I), and a linear tear of 1 mm thickness on the medial articular surface (ICRS III). On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, prepatellar edema in the subcutaneous tissue is observed. The bone marrow is evaluated with normal signal intensity. A moderate amount of intra-articular effusion is observed with extension into a Baker's cyst of craniocaudal diameter ~6 cm in the medial popliteal fossa.

Technique
The examination was performed on a 1.5T magnetic field strength MRI scanner, using a multi-channel coil, with image acquisition using T1-weighted and proton density sequences with fat signal suppression.

Findings
A small fluid collection is identified in the knee joint. The medial meniscus, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, have normal signal intensity and morphology. Abnormal signal is observed in the body of the lateral meniscus. The bone marrow has normal signal intensity in the distal femur and proximal tibia and fibula. The articular cartilage in the medial and lateral compartments does not show findings of injury or degeneration. On evaluation of the anterior compartment and the extensor mechanism, the quadriceps and patellar tendons appear normal, and the patella has normal morphology and position relative to the femoral trochlea. The articular cartilage along the medial facet of the inferior pole of the patella shows significant thinning (ICRS stage IV) with a small subarticular osteomyelitic lesion. A cystic lesion with a craniocaudal diameter of 3.5 cm is observed adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle.

Conclusion
Early degenerative osteoarthritis of the anterior compartment with joint effusion and Baker's synovial cyst. Degeneration, without tear, of the lateral meniscus.

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS

From the evaluation of the medial compartment, findings of extensive degenerative osteoarthritis are observed with total erosion of the articular cartilage (ICRS stage 4), degenerative tear and extrusion of the medial meniscus, presence of marginal osteophytes and subarticular bone marrow edema on both sides of the joint.

From the evaluation of the lateral compartment, simple degeneration without tear of the lateral meniscus is observed, with presence of marginal osteophytes without significant erosion of the articular cartilage.

From the evaluation of the anterior compartment, presence of large osteophytes in the region of the anterior femur is noted, without however substantial erosion of the articular cartilage of the patella.

Intra-articularly, joint effusion is observed with presence of a loose body in the anterior part of the joint with a transverse diameter of 11 mm.

The bone marrow presents benign hypertrophy.

In the intercondylar notch, new bone formation is observed, particularly prominent in the medial part of the lateral femoral condyle, with accompanying total tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, most likely due to chronic impingement.

In the posterior part of the medial femoral condyle, the large osteophyte projecting laterally presents bone marrow edema, most likely due to impingement on the surrounding muscles and tendons.

No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

Diffuse superficial chondropathy of the patella.
No significant joint effusion or popliteal cysts.

Impression:
Diffuse superficial chondropathy of the patella.
Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis.
Probable friction phenomena of the pes anserine tendons at the level of the medial tibial plateau.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss with superimposed foci of full-thickness chondral fissuring with subchondral cystic change and marrow edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal high-grade chondral fissuring at the inferomedial trochlea and trochlear notch.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Thickening of the medial collateral ligament, likely reflecting scarring from prior injury. No edema to indicate an acute injury.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis with intrasubstance signal alteration at the medial insertion.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 9 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Moderate medial compartment and mild patellofemoral compartment chondrosis.
2. Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis.
3. No meniscal tear.

Patellar cartilage with mild superficial irregularity at the apex of the patella. Trochlear cartilage with preserved thickness and signal. Thickening with signal abnormality of the proximal patellar tendon.
Remaining regional tendons with preserved thickness and signal.
Mild joint effusion. No Baker's cyst is observed.

Bone contusion foci in the described sites associated with grade I-II sprain of the anterior tibiofibular ligament.

Indication: Anterior right knee pain.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.  

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: 
Bone marrow edema identified in the patella which appears related to full-thickness chondrosis. There are tricompartment marginal osteophytes. 
Alignment is anatomic.  No aggressive osseous lesions.  

JOINT SPACE: 
Intra-articular body deep to the posterior root of the medial meniscus. Small joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Medial meniscus: Extensive complex tear of the meniscus with partial tearing of the posterior root, maceration of the posterior horn, and undersurface tearing body. 
Medial compartment cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage loss posterior weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle. Button osteophyte/articular spur of the femoral condyle. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Diffuse intrasubstance degeneration with no tear. 
Lateral compartment cartilage: Small areas of full-thickness cartilage loss on both sides of the joint. Button osteophyte/articular spur of the femoral condyle.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.  
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.  

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy.  Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact. 

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

MRI findings: Right knee joint: No MRI evidence of joint effusion. The bones forming the knee joint have preserved shape. Osteophytic deposits are seen on the patella – supratrochlear on the left, with lateral subluxation of the patella. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is thinned with erosions of the patellar cartilage and small subchondral bone cysts along its posterior margin with adjacent perifocal edema. An oblique defect of short extent in the cartilage of the medial condyle of the right femur in the zone of maximum loading, without underlying subchondral bone lesion. Subchondral bone cysts (geodes) are seen beneath the intercondylar eminences, which are sharpened. Similar small cysts are also seen at the level of the tibiofibular joint. Normal appearance of the cruciate ligaments. Degenerative changes are visualized in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Normal appearance of the lateral meniscus. Collateral ligaments – normal appearance. Patellar ligament, quadriceps femoris tendon – unremarkable. Popliteal fossa – unremarkable. Left knee joint: Status post partial meniscectomy and osteochondroplasty [DATE]. MRI evidence of early degenerative changes in the left knee joint. Small osteophytes are visualized along the articular margins of the femur and tibia, predominantly on the medial condyles. The intercondylar eminences are sharpened. Presence of an osteochondral defect in the anterior half of the medial femoral condyle with extensive bone marrow edema, outside the zone of maximum loading. A defect is seen in the overlying articular cartilage at this level. In the remaining areas, the articular cartilage of the tibia and femur has preserved congruence, mildly thinned. The anterior cruciate ligament is intact. Posterior cruciate ligament – unremarkable. Normal appearance of the lateral meniscus with early degenerative changes in its posterior horn. A rupture with horizontal to oblique course is visualized in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2b. Collateral ligaments – normal appearance of the medial collateral ligament. Degenerative changes at the insertions of the lateral collateral ligament, which is intact. The patella shows signs of chondromalacia. A small midline defect is seen in the articular cartilage in the region of the superior pole in combination with edematous subchondral changes in the adjacent posterior surface of the patella. The finding corresponds to chondromalacia – grade IV by Outerbridge grading system. Retinacula – unremarkable. Normal appearance of the soft tissues. Conclusion: Right knee joint: MRI evidence of trochlear dysplasia – type B by Dejour. Lateral subluxation of the patella. Early gonarthrotic changes with chondromalacia of the patella.

LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior and posterior horns and body of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus is extruded 5.5 mm medially from the knee joint space. Volume loss, maceration, and complex tear are observed in the meniscus. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain is observed in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Central-marginal osteophyte formation is observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint, mild sclerosis and edema in the subchondral area of the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint are observed. Destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilages is observed at this level. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis. A 2 cm diameter ossified lesion is observed in the posterosuperior vicinity of the supracondylar level of the femur in the popliteal fossa. Increased fluid and ossified nodular lesions, the largest being 1 cm in diameter, are also observed in the vicinity of the popliteus tendon.
CONCLUSION:
Gonarthrosis.
Medial extrusion, maceration, and complex tear of the medial meniscus.
Grade II meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus.
Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament.
Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament.
Suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint.
Synovial chondromatosis in the vicinity of the popliteus.
The ossified lesion in the popliteal fossa is interpreted in favor of chondromatosis.

Interpretation:

Minimal intra-articular effusion that could be physiological in nature. Large Baker's cyst that has progressed significantly in the interval, measuring 2.8 x 2.6 x 7.1 cm, with significant inferior extension along the medial gastrocnemius muscle with multiple fluid loculations and edema, suggesting an associated partial rupture.

In the interval, there is a slightly complex tear of the medial meniscus with maceration/radial component at the junction of the posterior horn and meniscal body as well as a potentially horizontal longitudinal component extending from the junction of the posterior horn with the meniscal body to the anterior horn and the superior articular surface. Significant meniscal extrusion with possibly a small displaced meniscal flap within the superior gutter of the medial femorotibial joint space, in contact with the deep meniscofemoral component of the medial collateral ligament. Mild edema at the periphery of the medial collateral ligament, reactive or related to a grade 1 sprain.

There is progression of degenerative changes/chondropathy in the femorotibial compartment, now moderate to severe, with full-thickness chondral fissures at the weight-bearing and non-weight-bearing surfaces (posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle). Minimal/early reactive subchondral changes at the medial aspect of the weight-bearing surface. Moderate marginal osteophytes.

The lateral meniscus is grossly unchanged without significant tear. The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact without tear. Mild degenerative changes/chondropathy in the lateral femorotibial compartment with diffuse attenuation of the articular surfaces.

Mild attenuation of the anterior cruciate ligament with mild signal abnormality without significant tear. This could be related to a prior low-grade sprain. No full-thickness tear. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact without tear. Small intraosseous ganglion cysts beneath its distal insertion at the posterior aspect of the tibia, increased in the interval.

The patella is high-riding. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact without tear. Again, severe degenerative changes/chondropathy at the medial aspect of the patellofemoral compartment, slightly more marked than on the previous study, with full-thickness attenuation of the cartilage surfaces and associated reactive subchondral changes. Small marginal osteophytes.

Conclusion:

In the interval, slightly complex tear of the medial meniscus as detailed above.

Progression of tricompartmental degenerative changes/chondropathy, moderate to severe in the medial femorotibial compartment and severe at the medial aspect of the patellofemoral compartment as detailed above.

Progression of a (large) Baker's cyst with signs of partial rupture.

Other findings as described above.

Alignment is anatomic. Multiple areas of curvilinear serpiginous high T2 and low T1 signal intensity are noted in the distal femoral metadiaphysis as well as in the medial femoral condyle and proximal medial tibia with central areas of fat, characteristic for osteonecrosis. The largest in the femur measures up to 4.8 cm mediolateral by 2.5 cm anterior posterior by 7.1 cm craniocaudal dimension, with a thick peripheral rim of enhancement and central areas of fat signal intensity. These findings are age-indeterminate with a probable chronic component given the central fat and absence of surrounding geographic marrow edema. Very subtle periarticular edema is noted along the anteromedial aspect anterolateral aspect of the femoral condyles. There is mild nonspecific marrow edema and a patella. Mild marrow edema is noted at the anterior patella and deep to the popliteus tendon. No aggressive osseous lesions.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. No significant joint effusion or erosive changes to suggest septic arthritis or inflammatory arthropathy. 

2. Multiple moderate to large areas of signal abnormality in the distal femur and proximal tibia demonstrating characteristic serpiginous high T2 and low T1 signal intensity, characteristic for areas of osteonecrosis. Mild marrow edema and enhancement deep to the popliteus tendon. These findings may represent stress-related changes or early developing areas of osteonecrosis.

Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: A lesion with a narrow transition zone, well-defined margins, approximately 15x11 mm in size, located in the distal diaphysis of the femur within the imaged section, hypointense on T1-weighted sequences and heterogeneous in intensity on T2-weighted sequences was observed. Enchondroma was primarily considered in the differential diagnosis of the lesion. Osteophytic spurring was noted in the bony structures forming the knee joint. Bone marrow edema was noted in the medial tibial plateau. The knee joint space is narrowed medially. Grade I chondromalacia was noted in the patellofemoral cartilage, particularly in the medial aspect. The integrity and signal intensity of the quadriceps and patellar tendons, lateral collateral ligaments, and posterior cruciate ligaments are normal. Decreased caliber of the anterior cruciate ligament was observed. Signal increase consistent with grade I sprain was noted in the medial collateral ligament. A complex tear in the anterior horn of the medial meniscus and meniscal extrusion beyond the joint were noted. Grade II degeneration was observed in the posterior horn. Grade II degeneration was observed in the anterior and posterior horns of the lateral meniscus. Increased effusion was observed in the joint space and suprapatellar bursa. An edematous appearance is present in the prepatellar soft tissue.

MCL.evidence: Signal increase consistent with grade I sprain was noted in the medial collateral ligament.

Medial Meniscus.evidence: A complex tear in the anterior horn of the medial meniscus and meniscal extrusion beyond the joint were noted.

Lateral Meniscus.evidence: Grade II degeneration was observed in the anterior and posterior horns of the lateral meniscus.

Medial OA.evidence: The knee joint space is narrowed medially. Osteophytic spurring was noted in the bony structures forming the knee joint. Bone marrow edema was noted in the medial tibial plateau.

Lateral OA.evidence: Osteophytic spurring was noted in the bony structures forming the knee joint.

Clinical History:
Synovitis of the right knee.

Findings:
Cruciate and collateral ligaments without alterations.
Extensive degenerative tear of the anterior horn, body, posterior horn, and part of the meniscal root of the lateral meniscus with significant associated extrusion.
Marginal tear of the body of the medial meniscus with minimal extrusion.
Full-thickness chondral ulcers with secondary bone changes and peripheral bone proliferations of the lateral femorotibial compartment. Partial-thickness and near full-thickness chondral ulcers of the weight-bearing zone of the medial femorotibial compartment.
Advanced degenerative changes of the patellofemoral joint with secondary bone changes and peripheral bone proliferations.
Moderate joint effusion with moderate diffuse synovitis associated with small diffuse intra-articular bodies. Multilobulated popliteal cyst, without signs of rupture.
Quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.

Impression:
Extensive degenerative tear of the lateral meniscus with associated extrusion.
Marginal tear of the medial meniscus with minimal extrusion.
Chondropathy with advanced degenerative changes of the lateral femorotibial and patellofemoral compartments.
Chondropathy grade two and three lesions of the medial femorotibial compartment.
Moderate joint effusion with moderate diffuse synovitis. Small diffuse intra-articular bodies. Uncomplicated popliteal cyst.

Diagnostic question: etiology

Findings:
Patellar cartilage damage, grade 2, with multiple superficial fissures.
Minimal joint effusion.
Femorotibial lateral cartilage damage, grade 2, characterized by heterogeneous signal and superficial fissures.
Mildly degenerative appearance of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with linear T2 hyperintense signal, possibly in contact with the inferior surface of the meniscus.

Infiltrated appearance of the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad, T2 intermediate signal.
Mildly thickened appearance of the proximal patellar tendon (anteroposterior diameter of 6.5 mm).

Conclusion:
Early degenerative abnormalities of the right knee with:
- Patellar cartilage damage grade 2
- Femorotibial lateral cartilage damage grade 2
Hoffa's fat pad syndrome.

Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in the proximal third with anterior tibial translation of approximately 10 mm.
Subtotal rupture of the medial collateral ligament extending obliquely through the ligament fibers.
Partial rupture of the lateral collateral ligament.
Partial rupture of the iliotibial tract at the tibial insertion with soft tissue edema adjacent to the LCL complex.
Normal morphology and signal intensity of the posterior cruciate ligament, patellar ligament, and quadriceps tendon.
The medial meniscus is of altered morphology and signal intensity, possibly representing an intrasubstance tear, differential diagnosis degenerative changes.
There is intrasubstance increased signal intensity of the anterior horn and root of the lateral meniscus – contusion with a horizontal tear of the anterior horn and part of the body of the lateral meniscus extending to the femoral articular surface.
Partial rupture of the anterior root of the lateral meniscus.
The patella is laterally subluxated. On the medial side of the medial patellar facet, there is a free crescent-shaped hypointense substrate measuring 7 mm – hemorrhage? meniscal fragment?
The articular cartilages are of normal signal intensity.
Knee joint effusion. No popliteal (Baker's) cyst is found. A small amount of loculated fluid adjacent to the pes anserinus tendons.
Extensive subcutaneous edema of the entire knee joint.
The other visualized osseous, soft tissue, and neurovascular structures are of normal morphology and signal intensity.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo.

FINDINGS
From the examination of the anterior compartment, a single superficial erosion of the articular cartilage of the medial surface of the patella is observed, without other lesions.
In the medial compartment, subarticular bone marrow edema and accompanying undulating erosions of the articular cartilage are identified, located on the surface of the medial femoral condyle and to a greater degree on the surface of the medial tibial condyle (ICRS grade 3), and presence of small marginal osteophytes on the medial tibial plateau.
The medial meniscus shows degeneration and subluxation.
A significant amount of joint effusion and synovitis is noted.
From the examination of the lateral compartment and the lateral collateral and cruciate ligaments, no significant pathological findings are noted.

CONCLUSION
Degenerative osteoarthritis of the medial compartment of the right knee with degenerative tear of the medial meniscus and joint effusion.

Mucoid degeneration of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus which appears attenuated and partially extruded. There is a small horizontal tear of the body which breaches the inferior meniscal surface.  Normal appearance of the pes anserine tendons, popliteus tendon, distal biceps femoris tendon and distal iliotibial band.  
Intact quadriceps and patellar tendons. Slight lateralization of the patellar relative to the trochlear groove. Trochlear dysplasia with a shallow trochlear groove noted. Normal T T - T G and patellar tendon ratio.  Focal high grade chondral thinning along the posterior aspect of the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle and lateral retropatellar facet. Relatively well-maintained lateral tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage.  
Conclusion:  -    Mucoid degeneration of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus which appears attenuated and partially extruded. There is a small horizontal tear of the body which breaches the inferior meniscal surface. -    Ancillary findings above.

[DATE]. 

Stable looking undersurface horizontal tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with no accompanying medial meniscal extrusion of note, nor is there any involvement of the corresponding posterior root and ligament.

An undisplaced degenerative tear of the free edge of the body and anterior horn of the lateral meniscus is again seen, together with lateral meniscal body extrusion.

Focal full-thickness articular cartilage loss noted at the junction between the central and posterior thirds of the lateral femoral condyle, with no accompanying fracture lines or mass lesions, nor any articular surface collapse.

Generalized thinning of medial and lateral weightbearing articular cartilage damage, with focal grade 3/4 articular cartilage loss being centred on the median ridge of the patella.

Moderate suprapatellar effusion, there are no intra-articular bodies.
A high-riding patella is also noted, together with patellofemoral incongruity and subtle superolateral Hoffa's fat pad impingement - the patellar lateralization present is not deemed secondary to the underlying effusion.

Small, non ruptured Baker's cyst noted posteromedially.

Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments, extensor tendons, distal iliotibial band and popliteus musculotendinous unit.

No other skeletal abnormality of note.
Grossly unremarkable remaining imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

Impression:
Medial and lateral meniscal pathology, age commensurate tricompartmental articular degenerative changes, multifactorial extensor mechanism abnormalities.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] female for right knee pain that is functional impairment. Mild OA on x-ray, but pain persistent/worsening.   .

PRIOR IMAGING: Bilateral knee ultrasound [Date].
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism are intact. The patellar cartilage is intact. The trochlear cartilage is intact. The patellar soft tissues normal.

The TT-TG interval measures 5 mm, within normal limits.

The anterior cruciate, posterior cruciate, medial collateral and lateral collateral ligament is complex, including the fibular lateral collateral ligament, iliotibial band, biceps femoris and popliteus tendons, are intact. No significant anterior tibial translation. Mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Medial meniscus is intact.  Articular cartilage of the medial femoral condyle is uniformly reduced in thickness.

Lateral meniscus anterior horn complex radial tear, posterior horn radial tear. Articular cartilage lateral of the femoral condyle is uniformly reduced in thickness.

Small suprapatellar knee joint effusion. 1.5 x 1.5 x 3.9 cm Baker's cyst.

Marrow signal is normal. Soft tissues is normal. Bone-on-bone articulation in the lateral compartment.

INTERPRETATION: 
Lateral meniscus anterior and posterior horn radial tears. Notably, the anterior horn demonstrates a complex radial tear while the posterior horn demonstrates a simple radial tear.

Uniform thinning of the bilateral femoral condyle articular cartilage, likely age-related etiology.

Baker's cyst. Bone-on-bone articulation in the lateral compartment.

- Findings of osteoarthritis of the left knee (medial and anterior compartment of the joint) with osteochondral lesions up to ICRS 4.

Interpretation:

There is a minimal rim of fluid in the lateral suprapatellar recess, unchanged, most likely related to a physiological accumulation. There is no significant intra-articular effusion. There is a small elongated Baker's cyst, unchanged, extending approximately 4 cm in craniocaudal diameter. There is no sign of complication.

The medial meniscus is unchanged, with no tear noted. There are mild degenerative changes in the medial femorotibial compartment with superficial chondral fissures, chondral attenuation, particularly at the weight-bearing surface, and small marginal osteophytes. There is a new small focus of non-specific edema at the posteromedial tibial plateau, on the more central aspect, non-specific. There is no fracture line or trabecular impaction noted. This could represent a small bone contusion or reactive changes related to the distal insertion of the posterior cruciate ligament in proximity.

The medial collateral ligament is intact and without tear.

The lateral meniscus is unchanged, with no tear noted. There are minimal degenerative changes in the lateral femorotibial compartment with mild chondral attenuation and early osteophyte formation at the joint margins.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact and without tear.

The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact and without tear. Again, there is a small intraosseous ganglion cyst beneath the insertion at the level of the tibial spines.

There are new foci of reactive subchondral changes at both aspects of the proximal tibiofibular joint, most likely of degenerative nature.

There is, again, lateral tilt/subluxation of the patella as well as large enthesophytes/ossifications at the origin of the patellar tendon. There is mild progression of marked diffuse thickening of the patellar tendon, particularly at the proximal third, compatible with underlying severe tendinosis. In the interval, there is a new focal proximal intrasubstance partial tear at the origin of the patellar tendon beneath the inferior pole of the patella, with slight caudal displacement of an ossification, potentially of avulsive nature. This appears intermediate to high grade, involving more than 50% of the tendon thickness at the origin of the tendon, with the main component measuring approximately 11 x 12 x 10 mm.

The previously described partial intrasubstance tear at the distal insertion involving the deep fibers of the patellar tendon appears resolved with mainly residual distal tendinosis.

There is mild reactive edema at the inferior pole of the patella. There is also associated infiltration of Hoffa's fat pad.

There is minimal residual prepatellar and infrapatellar thickening, without a frank bursitis component on the current study.

Furthermore, there are mild degenerative changes in the patellofemoral compartment with superficial chondral fissures. This is more marked at the patellar apex and the lateral patellar facet with small marginal osteophytes.

The patella is slightly high-riding with minimal edema also within the superolateral Hoffa's fat pad for which a friction syndrome between the patellar tendon and the lateral femoral condyle is suggested as previously mentioned.

The distal quadriceps tendon is intact and without tear.

Conclusion:

There is mild progression of already severe tendinosis involving the patellar tendon, particularly at its proximal third, as described above, with mainly a new focal partial tear potentially of avulsive type and of intermediate to high grade at its origin beneath the inferior pole of the patella as described above. There is mild reactive edema at the inferior pole of the patella.

There is interval resolution of a previously described tear distally within the patellar tendon.

There are new foci of reactive subchondral changes at the proximal tibiofibular joint, probably of degenerative nature, as well as a small bone contusion versus reactive changes at the slightly central aspect of the posterior medial tibial plateau as detailed above.

There is no other significant interval change.

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, PD fs, and T2me2d sequences.

FINDINGS:
Moderate amount of intra-articular fluid with accompanying thickening of the synovium in the lateral recesses of the joint. A small synovial cyst with a craniocaudal dimension of 4.5 cm is seen adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius. From the evaluation of the medial compartment, significant degeneration with presence of a tear in the posterior horn/adjacent to the posterior root of the medial meniscus and extrusion of the remaining meniscus is recognized. A displaced meniscal fragment is recognized adjacent to and anterior to the tibial insertion of the posterior cruciate ligament. The medial collateral ligament is depicted with mild thickening and focally pathological signal. Presence of bone edema (bone contusion) in the anterior part of the medial femoral condyle and the corresponding part of the lateral femoral condyle (kissing lesions), which topographically could correspond to a hyperextension injury. Additionally, significant erosion of the articular cartilage (ICRS stage III), marginal osteophytes, and anterior and posterior chondral osteophytes are recognized. Pathological signal is noted at the insertion of the semimembranosus muscle. The anterior cruciate ligament is recognized with horizontalization of its distal portion and pathological signal of its proximal portion where there is also blurring of its fibers. From the evaluation of the lateral compartment, mild degeneration of the meniscus and marginal osteophytes are recognized. A small ganglion cyst measuring 8 mm in diameter is noted anterior to the lateral meniscus. From the evaluation of the anterior compartment, an osteophyte at the superior and inferior margin of the articular surface of the patella and early chondropathy are recognized. Mild edema is noted within the prepatellar fat tissue.

CONCLUSION: Three-compartment osteoarthritis, of greater severity in the medial compartment. Coexisting mild synovitis. Tear of the medial meniscus and anterior cruciate ligament, and injury of the medial collateral ligament with accompanying bone edema (bone contusion), possibly in the setting of a hyperextension injury.

text:
MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
In the medial compartment, simple degeneration of the meniscus is observed without tear of it. Also, a marginal osteophyte is observed on the medial femoral condyle as well as a small defect of the articular cartilage, most likely of traumatic origin.

On examination of the lateral compartment, marginal osteophytes are also observed as well as degeneration of the lateral meniscus without findings of tear of it. The articular cartilage presents on the weight-bearing axis a focal defect of anteroposterior diameter 6mm and in the anterior portion of the lateral femoral condyle over an extent of approximately 2cm total erosion of the articular cartilage (ICRS grade 4) with subarticular osteomedullary edema.

On examination of the anterior compartment, total erosion of the articular cartilage of the lateral superior articular surface of the patella is observed (ICRS grade 4) with subarticular bone marrow lesions.

Intra-articularly, a large fluid collection is observed with focal projections of fatty tissue composition, while additionally a large synovial fold is observed in both the medial and lateral suprapatellar regions. A Baker's synovial cyst is observed in the popliteal fossa with findings of microtears of its wall. Incidentally, intra-articularly posterior to the medial femoral epicondyle, an osteochondral loose body of maximum diameter 6mm is observed.

CONCLUSION:
1. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the lateral compartment.
2. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the patellofemoral joint at its superior portion.
3. Hydrarthrosis with presence of secondary villous lipoma (lipoma arborescens) within it as well as a small loose body.

RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Central-marginal osteophyte formation was observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. The medial meniscus is extruded 6 mm medially from the knee joint. Volume loss, loss of integrity in the body segment, and grade III degeneration in the posterior horn were observed in the meniscus. Grade II degeneration in the anterior and posterior horn and body segment of the lateral meniscus, and a horizontal tear extending to the free edge were observed. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration was observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. Focal loss of cartilage integrity was observed in places on the medial facet of the patella. Increased fluid was observed in the suprapatellar bursa. Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral degenerative cysts, and subchondral edema were observed on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint. Destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilages is observed at this level. The findings were interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis.
Conclusion: Gonarthrosis. Medial extrusion of the medial meniscus, volume loss, loss of integrity in the body segment, grade III meniscopathy in the posterior horn. Grade II meniscopathy in the lateral meniscus with accompanying horizontal tear. Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade III chondromalacia of the medial facet of the patella. Suprapatellar bursitis.

Medial OA.evidence: Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral degenerative cysts, and subchondral edema were observed on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint. Destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilages is observed at this level.

Baker's.evidence: No popliteal cyst is mentioned; base-rate estimate in a degenerative knee with effusion.

Contusion.evidence: Subchondral edema were observed on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint. The findings were interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis.

Fracture.evidence: No fracture is described; subchondral cysts and sclerosis are attributed to degenerative arthritis.

Preserved articulation in the left knee joint. Known patella alta (Insall-Salvati 1.85) and unchanged laterally positioned patella. Progressive full-thickness cartilage defect at the patellar ridge and the lateral facet at the inferior patellar pole measuring approximately 1.5 x 1.0 cm. Adjacent intraosseous reactive edema (4/7). Also at the lateral femoral facet, partial full-thickness chondropathy (7/14). Single ossicle within the MPFL (7/10). However, no evidence of discontinuity of the ligament.
Preserved femorotibial articulation. Osteophytic formations predominantly at the lateral femoral condyle (4/18) and at the lateral tibial plateau (4/19), smaller osteophytes also in the medial compartment and femoropatellar.
Laterally femorotibial, segmentally thinned cartilage, exemplarily at the anterior aspect of the femoral condyles (5/23). In the medial compartment, largely preserved cartilage. Menisci intact without evidence of a tear. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus shows mildly increased signal on PD, differential diagnosis of initial mucoid changes. Cruciate ligaments also intact. Narrow fluid rim medial to the MCL, differential diagnosis of reactive state, no evidence of rupture. LCL unremarkable.
Small joint effusion. Synovium mildly thickened, minimally progressive Baker's cyst compared to 06/12 (3/97). Unremarkable appearance of the surrounding musculature and subcutaneous tissue.

RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
The medial meniscus is completely extruded medially by 9 mm from the knee joint space. Significant volume loss and complex tears are observed in the extruded meniscus. Grade III degeneration is observed in the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. The lateral collateral ligament is normal. Loss of continuity secondary to complete rupture is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Thinning and increased signal are observed in the proximal portion of the posterior cruciate ligament. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Cartilage destruction and bone marrow edema in the subchondral area are observed on the medial facet of the patella. Diffuse fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Central-marginal osteophytic formation is observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, edema, and degenerative cysts are observed on the bone surfaces adjacent to the medial tibiofemoral joint. Cartilage destruction is observed at these levels. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis. Cysts, the largest measuring 1 cm in diameter, are observed in the subcortical area at the insertion level of the cruciate ligaments on the anterior and posterior intercondylar eminence of the tibia. A Baker's cyst measuring 7x4 cm is observed in the popliteal fossa.
Conclusion: Gonarthrosis, medial extrusion of the medial meniscus, volume loss and complex tears, grade III meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus, complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament, diffuse thinning of the proximal posterior cruciate ligament, degenerative cysts of the tibial intercondylar eminence, suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint, grade 4 chondromalacia of the medial facet of the patella, Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa.

RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: A bucket-handle tear is observed in the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus is extruded 4.5 mm medially from the knee joint space. Grade II degeneration is noted in the posterior horn and body segment of the meniscus, with a horizontal tear at the free edge. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Thickening and increased signal secondary to mucoid degeneration are observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Periligamentous edema is noted in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and the knee joint space. Joint space narrowing is present in the medial tibiofemoral compartment, with millimetric osteophytic spurring at the corners of the bone structures adjacent to the joint. Thinning and destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilage are observed at this level. A Baker's cyst measuring 2.5 x 1 cm is noted in the popliteal fossa.
CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis. Medial extrusion and grade II meniscopathy of the medial meniscus. Bucket-handle tear of the lateral meniscus. Mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint.

MRI of left  Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, AX GRE T2*, Cor T2 FS, Screen Save

> Status of hemophilia B according to history
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with intermediate to mild hypointensity signal  on T1WI and heterogenous hyperintenisty signal inside, but no significant fluid-fluid interface,  C/W chronic hemarthrosis; suprapatellar and medial plicae.
    Irregular hypointensity signal material surround the joint capsule in left joint on all sequence, in favor of hypertrophy of the synovium with hemosiderin deposition ( especially at intercondylar region),  reflecting of hemophilic synovitis.
> Wearing of articular cartilage of left knee and mild mild subchondral bone edema and cysts over distal femur and tibial plateua; in favorof some  bone erosions.
> Suspicious of linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with suspicious of extending into the surface, R/O tear. 
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst, about 5 cm in length; [DATE] . Mild perifocal edema.
> Mild  subcutaneous edema over right knee and muscle edema over vastus medialis muscle.
> Subcutanoues edema and interstitial muscle edema over right proximal leg, more prominent in comparison with last MRI.
> Interstitial increased signal intensity of the muscles in left lower thigh, major at  anterior and posteror compartment of left lower thigh, including quadriceps muscles and biceps femoris muscle; in favor of intermusuclar hyperintensity area along biceps femoris muscle, maybe due to intermuscular edema/ hemorrhage .
    Minimal fluid accumulation in semimembranousus muscle and semitendinousus tendon
    
Impression: 
1. C/W hemophilic arthropathy of  left knee joint with prominent hemophilic synovitis and in favor of  chronic hemarthrosis and bulging of suprapatellar bursitis and Baker's cyst; patellar plicae.
2. [DATE]; in favor of some intermuscular edema/ hemorrahge along biceps femoris muscle.
3. R/O degeneration and tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

< IPSG MRI scale for haemophilic arthropathy >

*Soft tissue changes subscore: 9
    Effusion/haemarthrosis: Large (3)
    Synovial hypertrophy:  Large (3)
    Haemosiderin : Large (3)
*Osteochondral changes subscore:8
   Surface erosions involving subchondral cortex or joint margins
    Any surface erosion (1)
    Half or more of the articular surface eroded in at least one bone (1)
    Subchondral cysts At least one subchondral cyst (1)
    Subchondral cysts in at least two bones, or cystic changes involving 3 or more of the articular surface in at least one bone (1)
   Cartilage degradation
    Any loss of joint cartilage height (1)
    Loss of half or more of the total volume of joint cartilage in at least  one bone (1)
    Full-thickness loss of joint cartilage in at least some area in at least one bone (1)
    Full-thickness loss of joint cartilage including at least one half of the joint surface in at least one bone (1)

* Total score of IPSG MRI scale: [ID]

ACL.evidence: No mention of the ACL; report is focused on hemophilic arthropathy. Absence of any statement about ACL integrity leaves it indeterminate.

MCL.evidence: No mention of MCL injury. Only 'medial plicae' are noted, which is unrelated.

Medial Meniscus.evidence: Suspicious of linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with suspicious of extending into the surface, R/O tear.

Lateral Meniscus.evidence: No mention of lateral meniscus abnormality anywhere in the report.

Medial OA.evidence: Wearing of articular cartilage of left knee and mild subchondral bone edema and cysts over distal femur and tibial plateau; IPSG scale confirms full-thickness loss of joint cartilage including at least one half of the joint surface in at least one bone.

Lateral OA.evidence: Wearing of articular cartilage of left knee… subchondral cysts in at least two bones; IPSG osteochondral subscore 8 with full-thickness cartilage loss, consistent with diffuse hemophilic arthropathy affecting both tibiofemoral compartments.

PF OA.evidence: General 'wearing of articular cartilage of left knee' and IPSG cartilage degradation scores (full-thickness loss in at least some area) imply diffuse involvement; patellar plicae noted but no explicit PF cartilage description.

Effusion.evidence: Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis… C/W chronic hemarthrosis; IPSG scale: Effusion/haemarthrosis: Large (3).

Synovitis.evidence: Irregular hypointensity signal material surround the joint capsule… in favor of hypertrophy of the synovium with hemosiderin deposition… reflecting of hemophilic synovitis. IPSG: Synovial hypertrophy Large (3), Haemosiderin Large (3).

Baker's.evidence: A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst, about 5 cm in length.

Contusion.evidence: mild subchondral bone edema and cysts over distal femur and tibial plateau – in the setting of hemophilic arthropathy this is degenerative, not traumatic; intermuscular edema/hemorrhage along biceps femoris is spontaneous hemophilic bleeding rather than a traumatic contusion.

Fracture.evidence: No fracture described. 'Bone erosions' and 'subchondral cysts' are erosive/degenerative changes of hemophilic arthropathy, not fractures.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. No Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: Previously observed T2 weighted bright lesion located at the anteromedial distal femoral metadiaphysis shows no significant interval change in size. It currently measures approximately 1.1 cm x 1.4 cm x 1.6 cm in size. It has lobulated margins that shows a narrow zone of transition. No adjacent marrow edema is seen. No abnormal soft tissue component, cortical break nor abnormal periosteal reaction detected. Imaging findings are highly suggestive of a nonaggressive bony lesion, top differential diagnoses include a small bone cyst or a small or intraosseous ganglion. Interval increase in edema is also seen at the anterior medial tibia close to the insertion of the meniscal root, possibly due to traction or intraosseous ganglion. No fracture, stress reaction, or other osseous lesion is seen.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondrosis.

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal

Previously described T2 weighted bright lesion at the anterior aspect of the distal femoral metadiaphysis shows no significant with change compared with prior study, probably represents a nonaggressive lesion such as a small bone cyst or an intraosseous ganglion.

Minimal to mild chondrosis of the tibiofemoral joint and patellofemoral joint are similar to prior study.

Interval increase in edema is seen at the anteromedial tibia adjacent to the insertion of the anterior medial meniscal root, may represent an intraosseous ganglion.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo.

FINDINGS
From the evaluation of the medial compartment, degeneration and subluxation of the medial meniscus are observed, as well as a linear area of pathological signal in its posterior horn. The articular cartilage is satisfactorily evaluated.

In the lateral compartment of the knee, small marginal osteophytes are observed, as well as pathological signal of the lateral meniscus consistent with simple degeneration, without findings of tear. The articular cartilage has satisfactory depiction.

From the evaluation of the anterior compartment, thinning of the articular cartilage in places ICRS GRADE IV is observed, with presence of subcortical bone marrow lesions in the patella. A small fluid collection is observed intra-articularly.

The cruciate and collateral ligaments have normal appearance.

Large varicose venous dilations are observed at the anterior and posterior, especially lateral aspect of the knee.

A small focus of bone marrow edema is observed at the medial tibial epiphysis.

CONCLUSION:
1. Degenerative tear of the medial meniscus and small-scale microtrabecular insufficiency fractures at the medial tibial epiphysis, without depression of the articular surface.
2. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the anterior compartment at the patellofemoral articulation.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

 Lateral compartment

There are no normal intact fibers of the anterior cruciate ligament in keeping with a complete mid fiber tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear of mid fibers associated with a significant anterior tibial drawer.

Resolving kissing bone contusions in association with pivot shift mechanism of injury.

Complete radial tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus, with a large meniscal defect and marked degenerative changes of the remnant.

Marked joint effusion and chronic synovitis.
Signs of mucoid degeneration of the ACL.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the medial compartment, a degenerative tear of the medial meniscus is observed, in the presence of marginal osteophytes, erosion of the articular cartilage at the femoral and tibial condyles ICRS grade III, subarticular bone marrow edema on both sides of the joint space, and accompanying joint effusion. The findings are consistent with degenerative osteoarthritis.

In the lateral compartment of the knee, no significant findings are observed.

On evaluation of the anterior compartment, mild degenerative changes are observed with lateral marginal osteophytes on the patella and femoral trochlea, but without cartilage erosion. Intra-articularly, fluid collection is noted which contains small structures of fatty tissue. The finding corresponds to lipoma arborescens. The bone marrow shows benign hyperplasia.

In the popliteal fossa, a venous aneurysm is observed approximately 8 cm in length.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Moderate joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst. Large intra-articular organized soft tissue hematoma measuring 5.2 x 1.5 x 5.8 cm.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal medial collateral ligament with full-thickness tearing of the deep meniscofemoral ligament.
Longitudinal horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with mild loss of substance of the posterior horn.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Complete avulsion of the biceps femoris from the fibular head associated with a large multiloculated soft tissue hematoma surrounding the tear extending along the lateral gastrocnemius muscle.
Complete avulsion of the popliteus tendon at its insertion on the lateral femoral condyle.
Severe edema and irregularity of the lateral collateral ligament proper with high-grade partial-thickness tear from its femoral attachment and complete avulsion from its fibular attachment.
No fracture of the fibular head is identified.

Longitudinal vertical tear of the peripheral posterior horn and body of lateral meniscus.
Diffuse chondral thinning without deep fissuring.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. Avulsion of the posterior cruciate ligament from its femoral attachment.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Normal.

Bones:
Osteochondral impaction fracture of the medial femoral condyle/trochlea associated with underlying bone marrow reactive changes/contusions.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Diffuse edema of the visualized proximal anterior compartment of the leg muscles. Associated diffuse thickening and increased signal intensity of the common peroneal nerve suggesting traumatic injury without fiber discontinuity or transection.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:

1.Sequela of knee dislocation with complete tears of the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments.
2.Extensive injury of the posterolateral corner with complete avulsion of the lateral collateral ligament proper, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon as described above.
3.High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal medial collateral ligament with complete tearing of the deep meniscofemoral ligament.
4.Longitudinal horizontal tear of the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with mild substance loss of the posterior horn.
5.Longitudinal vertical peripheral tear of the posterior horn and body of lateral meniscus compatible with a Wrisberg rip.
6.Osteochondral impaction fracture of the medial femoral condyle/trochlea associated with underlying bone marrow reactive changes/contusions.
7.Diffuse thickening and increased signal intensity of the common peroneal nerve suggesting low-grade traumatic injury without fiber discontinuity or transection. Associated denervation edema of the visualized anterior muscle compartment of the proximal leg.
8.Moderate knee joint effusion with large intra-articular organized hematoma

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] female with trauma during ski accident 1.5 weeks ago with persistent pain, swelling and limited range of motion of left knee.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is a complete tear of the midportion of the anterior cruciate ligament. No normal intact fibers are identified. There is a borderline anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment at about 5 mm. There are bone contusions seen at the lateral femoral sulcus in the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau consistent with kissing contusions related to a pivot shift mechanism of injury. There is a discrete region of linear low T1 signal along the posterior rim of the lateral tibial plateau which may indicate presence of an undisplaced lateral tibial plateau rim fracture.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

There is abnormal signal surrounding the medial collateral ligament at its origin along its course proximal to the medial joint line consistent with grade 2 sprain. There is significant disruption of the deep fibers with intact superficial fibers extending distally. The posterior oblique ligament appears intact. There is an associated partial thickness sprain of the femoral insertion of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact. There is some subtle increased signal seen in the proximal fibers of the fibular collateral ligament which could indicate presence of a low-grade sprain. The fibular collateral ligament, IT band, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is abnormal increased T2 signal seen in the periphery of the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body consistent with a meniscocapsular avulsion injury. No discrete surfacing meniscal tear is identified to the medial meniscus. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact. The lateral patellofemoral ligament is unremarkable. As noted the medial patellofemoral ligament at its femoral insertion demonstrates a partial thickness sprain. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is reasonably well-maintained apart from some mild fissuring seen to the trochlear articular cartilage at the apex and involving the medial facet. Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis.

No significant Baker's cyst is demonstrated.

There is a moderate to large knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION:
 
Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear with bone contusions corresponding to a pivot shift mechanism of injury and with possible undisplaced posterior tibial plateau fracturing. Plain film correlation is recommended.

Grade 2 medial collateral ligament sprain associated with partial-thickness sprain of the insertional fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

Evidence of meniscocapsular injury to the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body with no discrete surfacing tear identified.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Moderate knee effusion.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo.

FINDINGS:
There is an area of low signal on T1 sequence (1.2 x 0.7 cm) in the region of the medial femoral condyle – medial compartment, subchondrally, with a fracture line on PdFS sequence and surrounding bone marrow edema. The findings are attributed to a microtrabecular insufficiency fracture (synonym of "spontaneous osteonecrosis"). There is coexisting reactive edema of the medial collateral ligament. A similar lesion, of lesser extent, is observed in the lateral portion, near the midline, of the tibial epiphysis. Increased amount of intra-articular fluid is noted. The lateral meniscus is depicted with diffusely increased signal in the setting of a degenerative tear. On evaluation of the menisci, simple degeneration without tear is observed. The articular cartilage in the medial and lateral compartments has satisfactory appearance. On evaluation of the anterior compartment, lateral subluxation of the patella is observed, with erosion of the articular cartilage ICRS grade 4, presence of small subchondral bone marrow lesions, and accompanying joint effusion.
Conclusion: The findings are consistent with degenerative osteoarthritis of the patellofemoral joint.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.
FINDINGS
RIGHT KNEE
On evaluation of the lateral compartment, degenerative tear of the lateral meniscus and subluxation of the latter are observed, erosion of the articular cartilage ICRS grade 4, presence of marginal osteophytes, and small subchondral bone marrow lesions of the lateral femoral condyle. On evaluation of the medial compartment, degeneration of the meniscus without tear is observed, presence of osteophytes, and mild erosion of the articular cartilage. On evaluation of the anterior compartment, lateral subluxation of the patella is observed with erosion of the articular cartilage ICRS grade 4 at the lateral articular surface and presence of subchondral bone marrow lesions. Intra-articularly, joint effusion is observed with presence of small cartilaginous loose bodies. In the intercondylar notch, osteophytic formations are observed accompanied by myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament secondary to impingement syndrome. Additionally, on evaluation of the articular cartilage, extensive chondrocalcinosis is observed in the context of CPPD.
Conclusion: Degenerative osteoarthritis of the lateral and anterior compartments.

text: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: The lateral meniscus and medial menisci are extruded from the joint space with significant volume loss, maceration, and grade III degeneration observed in the menisci. Loss of continuity secondary to complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament is observed. The posterior cruciate ligament has a markedly buckled appearance. Central-marginal osteophyte formation is observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing in the medial and lateral tibiofemoral compartments, subchondral sclerosis, edema, and millimetric cysts on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint are observed. Destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilage is observed at this level. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis. Ossified nodular lesions, the largest measuring 7 mm in diameter, surrounded by synovial fluid are observed posterior to the knee joint, adjacent to the popliteus tendon sheath. Findings are interpreted in favor of synovial chondromatosis. A tear in the posterosuperior aspect of the knee joint capsule with an associated 2.5x1.5 cm ganglion cyst is observed. A 3x2 cm extra-articular ganglion cyst is observed posterior to the knee joint. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Anterior subluxation of the tibia from the tibiofibular joint is observed. The cartilage on the lateral facet of the patella is markedly thinned. Conclusion: Gonarthrosis. Extrusion, volume loss, maceration, and grade IIII meniscopathy in the medial and lateral menisci. Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament and buckled appearance of the posterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Tear of the posterior knee joint capsule and associated ganglion cysts. Suprapatellar bursitis and synovitis of the knee joint. Subluxation of the tibia. Degenerative changes of the attachment of the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle to the femur.
A small amount of effusion in the semimembranosus bursa.

Other findings within normal limits.

MRI findings: Small joint effusion is present. Osteophytes are seen along the lateral and medial articular margins of the tibia and femur, along the posterior surface of the medial tibial condyle, along the anterior surface of the lateral tibial condyle, along the femoral condyles anteriorly, and at both poles of the patella. The articular cartilage of the patella and femur is thinned in the lateral half of the patellofemoral joint. A well-defined zone of bone marrow edema is present in the patella on this side. No MRI evidence of chondromalacia of the patella. Subchondrally located bone cysts in the lateral femoral condyle. An intra-articularly located lesion of oval shape with low signal intensity on PD and PD SPAIR is seen. The finding measures 5/3 mm and is located behind the insertion site of the posterior cruciate ligament on the tibia. A small amount of fluid is present around the described finding. MRI evidence of a hyperintense lesion with horizontal course in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, which extends into the body and a portion of the anterior horn of the meniscus. Multilocular cyst of the lateral meniscus.
MRI evidence of a hyperintense lesion with oblique course in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, which reaches the edge of the meniscus, without visible contact with the articular surfaces of the tibia and femur. Normal appearance of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus. The cruciate ligaments are intact. Patellar retinacula, collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon and patellar ligament – with preserved integrity and signal intensity. Subcutaneous edema is present along the anterolateral surface of the leg.
Conclusion: MRI evidence of small joint effusion. Arthritic changes in the lateral half of the patellofemoral joint. Well-defined bone marrow edema in the patella. Joint loose body. Lesion in the posterior horn, body, and part of the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus – grade 2a. Cyst of the lateral meniscus. Lesion in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2a. Subcutaneous edema of the leg.

Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the lateral meniscus and medial meniscus. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The signal of the anterior cruciate ligament is diffusely increased and its integrity cannot be assessed secondary to complete rupture. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Mild fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa, at the level of the patellofemoral joint. Central-marginal osteophytic spurs are observed in the bony structures of all three compartments of the knee joint. Subchondral millimetric cysts are observed in the tibial intercondylar tubercle.

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Large, solid prepatellar mass. Chronic.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

There is a complex fluid collection within the prepatellar soft tissues, measuring 35 x 6 x 25 mm with internal hypodensity/T2 signal as well as a thick low proton density/low T2 signal rim (measuring 4 mm in thickness). The appearance is consistent with complex prepatellar bursitis. No other discrete mass lesion identified. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

The medial meniscus shows intrasubstance degeneration of the posterior horn without discrete tear. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

Medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, and biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear. The iliotibial band is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 13 mm, within normal limits.

There is fissuring and thinning of articular cartilage overlying the medial patellar facet. Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage.

Low proton density/low T2 signal lesion within the anterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle measuring 23 x 9 x 9 mm without aggressive imaging features, likely representing a bone island.

Small knee joint effusion. Regional musculature is within normal limits. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex prepatellar bursitis, with a thick walled, 56 x 6 x 25 mm collection noted in the prepatellar soft tissues.
2. Mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis.
3. Probable bone island medial femoral condyle; plain film correlation recommended for confirmation.
4. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear.

MCL.evidence: Medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, and biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact.

Synovitis.evidence: The appearance is consistent with complex prepatellar bursitis.

Baker's.evidence: No mention of a popliteal or Baker's cyst in the report.

Contusion.evidence: No bone marrow edema or contusion described; the low-signal lesion is attributed to a probable bone island.

Fracture.evidence: No fracture identified; the medial femoral condyle lesion is described as a probable bone island without aggressive features.

MRI RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
A significant joint effusion is observed in the knee joint, which communicates with a Baker's cyst adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle, with a craniocaudal diameter of approximately 5 cm.
On evaluation of the collateral ligaments, the posterior cruciate ligament, and the lateral meniscus, no pathological findings are observed.
Anterior to the medial collateral ligament, thickening and edema are observed in the medial patellofemoral ligament, a finding compatible with mild injury of it.
In the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus, a linear abnormality is observed extending to the articular surface.
The bone contusion that had been observed on the previous examination at the lateral tibial condyle is no longer seen.
The articular cartilage has normal appearance.
The anterior cruciate ligament shows thinning at its proximal and distal thirds.

CONCLUSION:
1. Partial chronic tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
2. Joint effusion and Baker's cyst.
3. Medial meniscus tear.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]
